member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Client.IMAP_Client
member.summary: Represents an IMAP4rev1 client capable of connecting to an IMAP server, authenticating a user, selecting mailboxes, retrieving messages, issuing IMAP commands, and managing server-side message state.

remarks.para: This client implements the core IMAP4rev1 protocol as defined in RFC 3501, including support for authentication, mailbox selection, message fetching, message copying, message flag manipulation, and folder listing. The client maintains a persistent TCP connection to the server and processes all IMAP responses according to the protocol's tagged and untagged response model.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Client.IMAP_Client.#ctor
member.summary: Default constructor.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Client.IMAP_Client.OnConnectedAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
Handles the initial IMAP server greeting received immediately after the TCP connection is established. According to RFC 3501 section 7.1.1, the server must send a single untagged status response beginning with the asterisk (*) tag. The greeting indicates whether the server is ready for authentication (OK), has pre-authenticated the session (PREAUTH), or is closing the connection (BYE).
This method reads the greeting line, verifies that it is an untagged status response (), and checks whether the status code represents an error condition. A greeting with a non-OK status code (NO, BAD, or BYE) results in an being thrown. For valid greetings, the human-readable greeting text is stored for later use.
member.param: A cancellation token that can be used to cancel the asynchronous operation.
member.exception: Thrown when the server greeting is not an untagged status response or when the greeting contains an error status code.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Client.IMAP_Client.Disconnect
member.summary: Disconnects from the IMAP server by invoking the asynchronous method with sendQuit set to true and waiting for its completion.

remarks.para: This synchronous wrapper creates a using the client's configured value and blocks until the asynchronous disconnect operation completes. The underlying method optionally sends the IMAP LOGOUT command, reads the server's final response, resets all session state, and closes the connection.
Any exceptions thrown by the asynchronous disconnect sequence are propagated to the caller of this method.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Client.IMAP_Client.DisconnectAsync(System.Boolean,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
Disconnects from the IMAP server and optionally sends the LOGOUT command before closing the underlying connection. According to RFC 3501 section 6.1.3, the LOGOUT command requests that the server terminate the session and return a final tagged status response, typically followed by an untagged * BYE notification.
When is true, this method sends a LOGOUT command using a new command tag and reads the server's final response. Any exceptions raised during transmission or reception of the logout sequence are suppressed, and the connection is closed regardless.

Protocol rules:

item.description: The server sends continuation prompts (+) containing base64-encoded challenge data.

remarks.para: The EXAMINE command selects a mailbox in read-only mode. The server MUST NOT permit any permanent state changes while the mailbox is examined. This includes flag updates, message deletions, keyword changes, and any operation that would alter the mailbox’s persistent state.

The server returns the same untagged responses as SELECT, including: FLAGS, PERMANENTFLAGS, EXISTS, RECENT, UIDVALIDITY, UIDNEXT, and optionally UNSEEN and HIGHESTMODSEQ. The tagged completion response MUST include [READ-ONLY] to indicate that the mailbox cannot be modified.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Client.IMAP_Client.EnableUtf8IfSupportedAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
Attempts to enable UTF‑8 related IMAP capabilities on the current connection using the IMAP ENABLE command (RFC 5161).
The method enables UTF‑8 features in a safe, RFC‑defined order and updates internal client state based on which capabilities the server actually activates.
member.param: A cancellation token that can be used to cancel the asynchronous operation.
member.returns: A task representing the asynchronous operation.
member.exception: Thrown when the client instance has already been disposed.
Thrown when the client is not connected, not authenticated, or is currently in the IDLE state.

remarks.para: The method checks the server's advertised capabilities and attempts to enable the following UTF‑8 related extensions in the recommended order: UTF8=ACCEPT, UTF8=RESP-CODES, UTF8=SEARCH, and UTF8=USER. Each capability is enabled using a separate ENABLE command to ensure deterministic behavior.
Only capabilities explicitly listed in the server's untagged ENABLED responses are considered active. A tagged OK response alone does not indicate that a capability was successfully enabled.

When UTF8=ACCEPT is enabled, the client switches mailbox name encoding to UTF‑8. When UTF8=SEARCH is enabled, the client allows UTF‑8 search keys. When UTF8=USER is enabled, the client permits UTF‑8 usernames and passwords for authentication.
The capabilities UTF8=ONLY and UTF8=ALL are intentionally not enabled automatically because they alter mailbox name semantics or are obsolete.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Client.IMAP_Client.FolderClose
member.summary: Executes the IMAP CLOSE command on the currently selected mailbox.
member.exception: Thrown if the client instance has already been disposed.
Thrown if the client is not connected, not authenticated, no mailbox is currently selected, or the client is in the IDLE state. The CLOSE command cannot be issued while IDLE is active.
Thrown when the server returns a tagged NO or BAD response, indicating that the mailbox could not be closed.

remarks.para: This method is the synchronous wrapper for . A cancellation token with the client’s configured timeout is created internally, and the asynchronous operation is executed synchronously using GetAwaiter().GetResult().

The CLOSE command permanently removes all messages in the selected mailbox that have the \Deleted flag set. The expunge is performed silently: the server MUST NOT send untagged EXPUNGE responses for the removed messages.

After expunging deleted messages, the server deselects the mailbox and returns to the authenticated (non-selected) state. No further commands may operate on the mailbox until a new SELECT or EXAMINE command is issued.

remarks.para: This method is a synchronous wrapper around . It blocks until the STORE operation completes.

RFC 3501 — STORE Command
The STORE command modifies message flags for the messages in the provided sequence set. Depending on the selected mode, the operation may replace the entire flag set, add new flags, or remove existing flags. Silent variants suppress untagged FETCH responses.

On success, the server returns a final tagged OK response. Non‑silent operations cause the server to send untagged FETCH responses containing updated flags. Silent operations suppress these responses.

list.item: STORE operates on message sequence numbers.
determines whether flags are replaced, added, or removed, and whether the operation is silent.
The flag list may be empty. For FLAGS, this clears all flags. For +FLAGS and -FLAGS, an empty list performs a no‑op.
The \Deleted flag marks a message as deleted but does not physically remove it.

RFC 3501 — COPY Command
The COPY command copies the messages identified by the provided sequence set to the end of the target mailbox. The source messages remain unchanged in the currently selected mailbox.

remarks.para: The capability list is populated from the server's CAPABILITY response, either from the initial greeting or from an explicit CAPABILITY command issued by the client. The values indicate which IMAP extensions, authentication mechanisms, and protocol features the server supports for the active session.
Accessing this property requires the client to be connected. If the client is not connected, an is thrown.
If the IMAP client has been disposed, accessing this property will throw an .
If the server has not advertised any capabilities, the property returns an empty array rather than null.

member.exception: Thrown if the IMAP client instance has been disposed.
Thrown if the client is not currently connected.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Client.IMAP_Client.SaslAuthMethods
member.summary: Gets the list of SASL authentication mechanisms advertised by the IMAP server for the current connection.

remarks.para: The returned array contains the SASL mechanism names extracted from capability tokens of the form AUTH=mechanism. These values are provided exactly as reported by the server and may include mechanisms such as PLAIN, LOGIN, CRAM-MD5, DIGEST-MD5, XOAUTH2, or other implementation‑specific extensions.
The list is derived from the server's CAPABILITY response. If the server does not advertise any AUTH= tokens, the property returns an empty array rather than null.
Accessing this property requires the client to be connected. If the client is not connected, an is thrown.
If the IMAP client has been disposed, accessing this property will throw an .

member.exception: Thrown if the IMAP client instance has been disposed.
Thrown if the client is not currently connected.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Client.IMAP_Client.SelectedFolder
member.summary: Gets the currently selected IMAP mailbox, or null if no mailbox has been selected for the active session.

remarks.para: The value is set when a SELECT or EXAMINE command completes successfully. Until that point, the property remains null. The returned instance exposes all server‑reported mailbox metadata and provides methods for creating message sets within the selected mailbox.
Accessing this property requires the client to be connected. If the client is not connected, an is thrown.
If the IMAP client has been disposed, accessing this property will throw an .

member.exception: Thrown if the IMAP client instance has been disposed.
Thrown if the client is not currently connected.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Client.IMAP_Client_Message
member.summary: Represents a single IMAP message within a selected mailbox. Instances of are created internally by from the results of a bulk FETCH operation and expose both prefetched and lazily retrieved message metadata.

remarks.para: A message object provides access to common IMAP metadata such as UID, size, internal date, flags, envelope, body structure, and (when enabled) Gmail‑specific extensions. Metadata that was not prefetched during message‑set creation remains null until explicitly retrieved using or .
In addition to metadata access, the class provides convenience methods for common per‑message IMAP operations such as copying, moving, flag manipulation, and retrieving the RFC 5322 header block.

The object does not perform any IMAP communication during construction. All prefetched values originate from the FETCH response that created the containing . Lazy retrieval methods perform targeted FETCH UID requests only when needed, and cache the results for subsequent access.
A message instance becomes invalid after disposal. Once disposed, any attempt to perform IMAP operations such as retrieving envelope or body structure will result in an .

member.summary: Synchronously moves this message to the specified target mailbox by performing a UID-based COPY followed by adding the IMAP \Deleted flag to the original message. item.description: UID COPY of this message to the target mailbox

member.param: The target mailbox name. Must not be null or empty.
A cancellation token that can be used to cancel the operation.

remarks.para: This method implements the standard IMAP MOVE fallback for servers that do not support the MOVE extension. The operation consists of:

item.description: UID COPY of this message to the target mailbox

remarks.para: No EXPUNGE is performed. This avoids unreliable sequence-number-based expunge notifications and ensures UID safety. The actual removal of the message occurs only when the mailbox is expunged (explicitly or implicitly on logout, depending on server behavior).

Safety considerations: IMAP literals include an explicit size prefix ({N}). Servers are expected to send exactly N bytes, but intermediary systems (spam filters, antivirus gateways, proxies) may rewrite message content without updating RFC822.SIZE. To guard against malformed or hostile server behavior, implementations should enforce an upper bound on the literal size. This client limits the allowed literal size to the message's reported RFC822.SIZE plus a 1 MB safety margin. Any literal exceeding this threshold is rejected to prevent excessive resource usage or protocol desynchronization.

Although most modern IMAP servers report UIDNEXT, the IMAP specification defines it as a SHOULD rather than a MUST. As a result, some legacy or non‑compliant servers may omit the value, and the property will remain null until explicitly set by the client's untagged‑response handler.
Accessing this property after the folder has been disposed will throw an .

member.exception: Thrown if this folder instance has been disposed.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Client.IMAP_Client_SelectedFolder.FirstUnseen
member.summary: Gets the message sequence number of the first unseen message in the selected mailbox, if reported by the server.

remarks.para: The value is taken from the server’s OK [UNSEEN n] response, returned during SELECT or EXAMINE. It indicates the lowest‑numbered message that does not have the \Seen flag.

If the server does not send an UNSEEN response, the property is null. This means only that the server did not report a first unseen message; clients may still determine unseen messages by examining individual message flags.
The value is a message sequence number (MSN), not a UID.

member.exception: Thrown if this message instance has been disposed.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Client.IMAP_Client_SelectedFolder.MessagesCount
member.summary: Gets the total number of messages currently present in the selected mailbox.

remarks.para: The value corresponds to the server’s untagged * EXISTS response, returned during the SELECT or EXAMINE command. It represents the number of messages in the mailbox at the moment the folder was selected.

The count may change during the session if new messages arrive or existing messages are expunged. Such changes are reported by additional untagged EXISTS or EXPUNGE responses, which update this property automatically through the client’s global untagged‑response handler.
The value is a message sequence number count (MSN‑based), not a UID count. It reflects the current ordering and numbering of messages within the selected mailbox.

member.exception: Thrown if this message instance has been disposed.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Client.IMAP_Client_SelectedFolder.RecentMessagesCount
member.summary: Gets the number of messages in the selected mailbox that have the \Recent flag set.

remarks.para: The value corresponds to the server’s untagged * RECENT response, returned during the SELECT or EXAMINE command. It indicates how many messages the server considers newly delivered since the last time the mailbox was opened by any IMAP session.

The \Recent flag is maintained by the server and is not persistent. Once a mailbox is opened, the server may clear the flag from messages or adjust the count. For this reason, RECENT is not a reliable indicator of new mail for long‑term synchronization; clients typically use UIDs instead.
The count may change during the session if the server sends additional untagged RECENT responses. Such updates are applied automatically through the client’s global untagged‑response handler.

member.exception: Thrown if this message instance has been disposed.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_ServerStatus.Parse(System.String)
member.summary:
Parses an IMAP server status response from a single response line. This method handles both:
Continuation requests (the "+" response), as defined in RFC 3501 section 7.5. These responses are untagged and indicate that the server expects additional data from the client, typically literal content.
Command completion responses (OK, NO, BAD, PREAUTH, BYE), as defined in RFC 3501 section 7.1. These responses are tagged and may contain at most one optional response code enclosed in square brackets (e.g. [UIDNEXT 123]).
The method does not process IMAP literals; status responses never contain literal data.
member.param: The raw IMAP response line received from the server.
member.returns: An instance representing the parsed IMAP response.
member.exception: Thrown when is null.
Thrown when the response line violates IMAP syntax, such as missing a command tag, missing a response code, or containing a malformed optional response code.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_ServerStatus.ToString
member.summary:
Returns the IMAP wire-format representation of this tagged status response. Tagged status responses begin with the client-supplied command tag (e.g. A001) followed by the status response code (OK, NO, BAD, PREAUTH, or BYE) as defined in RFC 3501 section 7.1.
If present, the optional response code is emitted inside square brackets (for example [UIDNEXT 123]) exactly as specified in RFC 3501 section 7.1.2. The remainder of the line is free-form human-readable response text. The returned string is terminated with CRLF and contains no IMAP literals, since status responses never include literal data.
member.returns: A CRLF-terminated IMAP status response line suitable for transmission to an IMAP client. Any braces or brackets appearing in the response text are emitted verbatim.

remarks.para: An ACL response reports the Access Control List entries associated with a specific mailbox. The response contains the mailbox name and zero or more identifier‑rights pairs, where each identifier represents a user, group, or special ACL subject, and each rights string specifies the permissions granted to that identifier.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_Capability
member.summary: Represents an untagged IMAP CAPABILITY response as defined in RFC 3501 section 7.2.1. A CAPABILITY response is sent by the server to announce the set of protocol features, extensions, authentication mechanisms, and server-specific tokens that it supports.

remarks.para: CAPABILITY responses are always untagged and begin with the asterisk (*) response tag followed by the atom CAPABILITY. The remainder of the line consists of zero or more capability atoms separated by whitespace. Each capability is a case-insensitive atom identifying a protocol feature such as IMAP4rev1, STARTTLS, LITERAL+, SASL-IR, or AUTH=PLAIN.

According to RFC 3501, CAPABILITY responses never contain IMAP literals, quoted strings, or multi-line data. All capability information appears on a single line. This class stores the capability atoms exactly as reported by the server without modification.
CAPABILITY responses may appear in the server greeting, in response to a client-issued CAPABILITY command, or at other times when the server wishes to inform the client of its supported features.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_Capability.#ctor(System.String[])
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class using the capability atoms supplied by the IMAP server. Each element in represents a single capability token as defined in RFC 3501 section 7.2.1.
member.param: The array of capability atoms parsed from the server's CAPABILITY response. Each entry must be a valid IMAP atom and must not contain literals, quoted strings, or multi-line data.

remarks.para: The IMAP CAPABILITY response is an untagged server response that advertises the set of protocol features, extensions, authentication mechanisms, and server-specific tokens supported by the server. Each capability is a case-insensitive atom and appears on a single line following the * CAPABILITY prefix.

This constructor stores the capability atoms exactly as provided by the parser. No normalization, filtering, or interpretation is performed. Clients may inspect the capability list to determine server features such as IMAP4rev1, STARTTLS, LITERAL+, SASL-IR, AUTH=PLAIN, IDLE, UIDPLUS, and other extensions.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_Capability.Parse(System.String)
member.summary: Parses an IMAP CAPABILITY response line into an instance. According to RFC 3501 section 7.2.1, a CAPABILITY response is an untagged server response beginning with the asterisk (*) tag followed by the atom CAPABILITY and zero or more capability atoms.

remarks.para: The CAPABILITY response lists the protocol features, extensions, authentication mechanisms, and server-specific tokens supported by the IMAP server. Each capability is a case-insensitive atom. The response never contains IMAP literals, quoted strings, or multi-line data; all capabilities appear on a single line separated by one or more whitespace characters.

This method validates the untagged response marker (*), the required CAPABILITY keyword, and then splits the remainder of the line into individual capability atoms. Empty or whitespace-only segments are removed. A is thrown if the response does not conform to the required syntax.

member.param: The raw IMAP response line beginning with * CAPABILITY.
member.returns: A new containing the parsed capability atoms.
member.exception: Thrown when is null.
Thrown when the response does not begin with * CAPABILITY or otherwise violates the CAPABILITY response grammar.

remarks.para: Each capability atom identifies a protocol feature, extension, authentication mechanism, or server-specific token supported by the IMAP server. The response is always a single line and never contains IMAP literals, quoted strings, or multi-line data.

This method emits the capability list exactly as stored in this instance, preserving the order and case of the capability atoms. The returned string is terminated with CRLF and is suitable for transmission to an IMAP client.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_Expunge
member.summary: Represents the IMAP EXPUNGE untagged server status response as defined in RFC 3501 section 7.4.1.
member.remarks:
The EXPUNGE response reports that the message with the specified sequence number has been permanently removed from the mailbox. After an EXPUNGE, all messages with higher sequence numbers are immediately decremented by one, and this renumbering is reflected in subsequent server responses.
An EXPUNGE response MUST NOT be sent when no command is in progress, nor while responding to a FETCH, STORE, or SEARCH command. It MAY be sent during UID FETCH, UID STORE, or UID SEARCH.
Clients MUST record updates from the EXPUNGE response.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_Flags
member.summary: Represents an untagged IMAP FLAGS response as defined in RFC 3501 section 7.2.6. A FLAGS response reports the complete set of flags that are applicable to the currently selected mailbox.

remarks.para: The FLAGS response is sent by the server as part of a SELECT or EXAMINE command. It contains a parenthesized list of all flags that may appear in messages within the mailbox.
At minimum, the server must include the standard system-defined flags: \Answered, \Flagged, \Deleted, \Seen, and \Draft. Servers may also include additional implementation-specific flags.
The client MUST record the update from the FLAGS response, as it defines the complete set of legal message flags for the mailbox.
Example server response: * FLAGS (\Answered \Flagged \Deleted \Seen \Draft)
This class stores the flags exactly as returned by the server. Interpretation and usage of the flags is left to the caller.
This class derives from , the base type for all untagged IMAP responses.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_List
member.summary: Represents a single untagged IMAP LIST response as defined in RFC 9051 section 7.2.2. A LIST response describes a mailbox available on the server, including its attribute list, hierarchy delimiter, and mailbox name.

remarks.para: The LIST response provides structural information about mailboxes matching the pattern supplied to the LIST command. Each response includes:

item.description: A list of mailbox attributes (for example \Noselect, \Marked, \HasChildren, \HasNoChildren).
A hierarchy delimiter, which is either a single character or NIL if no hierarchy delimiter is defined.
A mailbox name represented as an IMAP string. Depending on negotiated UTF-8 capabilities, non-ASCII mailbox names may be encoded either as UTF-8 or legacy modified UTF-7.

remarks.para: LIST responses describe mailbox hierarchy and mailbox attributes. They do not include subscription status, message counts, or mailbox status information.

The hierarchy delimiter returned by the server. This is either a single ASCII character when hierarchy is supported (for example '/' or '.'), or a null value when the server returns NIL, indicating that the mailbox does not support hierarchical child mailboxes.

The list of mailbox attributes returned inside the parentheses of the LIST response. Examples include \Noselect, \Marked, \Unmarked, \HasChildren, and \HasNoChildren. The array contains each attribute token exactly as provided by the server.

* LISTRIGHTS <mailbox> <identifier> <required-rights> [ <optional-rights> ... ]
Optional rights are emitted as individual IMAP atoms separated by spaces. If no optional rights are present, the optional rights portion of the response is omitted.
When is , mailbox names are encoded as required for IMAP servers that do not permit UTF-8 mailbox names in protocol responses.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_ListRights.FolderName
member.summary: Gets the name of the mailbox associated with this LISTRIGHTS response.

remarks.para: The folder name identifies the mailbox for which the server reports the rights that may be granted to a specific identifier. The value is returned exactly as provided by the server, after IMAP UTF‑7 decoding and removal of any surrounding quotes.
The folder name is never null. If the server sends an empty or syntactically invalid mailbox name, the parser will throw a .

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_ListRights.Identifier
member.summary: Gets the ACL identifier to which the rights in this LISTRIGHTS response apply.

remarks.para: The identifier represents the ACL subject for which the server reports the rights that may be granted. It may be a user name, group name, or a special IMAP ACL identifier such as anonymous or owner.

The value is returned exactly as parsed from the server response. If the server encoded the identifier as an IMAP literal, the literal payload is read and decoded before being stored. Quoted identifiers are unquoted, and atom identifiers are preserved as‑is.
The identifier is never null. If the server omits the identifier or provides an invalid literal header, the parser throws a .

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_ListRights.RequiredRights
member.summary: Gets the set of rights that the server reports as required for the identifier in this LISTRIGHTS response.

remarks.para: Required rights are those that MUST be granted if any rights are granted to the identifier. In most IMAP server implementations this value is an empty string, because few servers define rights that are inherently mandatory.
The value is returned exactly as parsed from the server response. It may be:

item.description: An empty string (""), which is the most common case.
A quoted empty string ("") in the raw response, which is normalized to an empty string.
A non‑empty rights string, if the server defines mandatory rights for the identifier.

remarks.para: The property is never null. If the server omits the required rights field entirely, the parser substitutes an empty string as permitted by RFC 4314.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_ListRights.OptionalRights
member.summary: Gets the set of optional rights that the server reports as rights which may be granted to the identifier in this LISTRIGHTS response.

remarks.para: Optional rights represent the complete set of rights that the server allows to be granted to the identifier for the specified mailbox. Each element in the array is a single rights character, such as l, r, w, or i, as defined in RFC 4314.
The LISTRIGHTS response may contain zero or more optional rights. If the server provides no optional rights, this property returns an empty array. The array is never null.
Optional rights are returned exactly as parsed from the server response. They are not concatenated or normalized; each rights token is preserved in the order provided by the server.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_LSub
member.summary: Represents a single untagged IMAP LSUB response as defined in RFC 3501 section 7.2.3. An LSUB response describes a mailbox to which the user is subscribed, including its attribute list, hierarchy delimiter, and decoded mailbox name.

remarks.para: The LSUB response is structurally identical to the LIST response, but differs in semantics: it reports only mailboxes that the user is subscribed to. Each response includes:

item.description: A list of attribute flags (for example \Noselect, \Marked, \HasChildren).
A hierarchy delimiter, which is either a single ASCII character or NIL when the server does not support hierarchical mailbox names.
A mailbox name encoded as a quoted string, which may contain modified UTF-7 and must be decoded.

remarks.para: Instances of this class are typically created by the Parse method, which interprets a raw LSUB response line and extracts the mailbox components.

The hierarchy delimiter returned by the server. This is either a single ASCII character (for example '/' or '.') when hierarchy is supported, or null when the server returns NIL, indicating that the mailbox namespace does not support hierarchical child mailboxes.

The list of mailbox attributes returned inside the parentheses of the LSUB response. Examples include \Noselect, \Marked, \Unmarked, \HasChildren, and \HasNoChildren. The array contains each attribute token exactly as provided by the server.

remarks.para: This constructor is typically used by the Parse method to represent a single untagged LSUB response as defined in RFC 3501 section 7.2.3.
The parameter uses a nullable character so that the IMAP NIL delimiter can be represented cleanly.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_MyRights
member.summary: Represents an IMAP MYRIGHTS untagged response as defined in RFC 4314. The response reports the set of rights that are currently in effect for the authenticated user for a specific mailbox.

remarks.para: A MYRIGHTS response provides the effective rights that the server grants to the authenticated user for a given mailbox. The response format is:

remarks.para: The folder name identifies the mailbox whose access rights are being reported. The value is returned after IMAP UTF‑7 decoding and removal of any surrounding quotes, preserving the exact mailbox name supplied by the server.
MYRIGHTS responses always contain a mailbox name, and this property is therefore never null. If the server omits the mailbox name or sends an invalid token, the parser throws a .

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_Namespace
member.summary: Represents an untagged IMAP NAMESPACE response as defined in RFC 2342. A NAMESPACE response describes the mailbox namespace structure available to the authenticated user, including personal, other‑users, and shared mailbox hierarchies.

remarks.para: The IMAP NAMESPACE command allows a client to discover how mailbox names should be constructed for different namespace categories. Each namespace category is represented by a list of namespace descriptors, where each descriptor contains a prefix and a hierarchy delimiter. These values are used by clients to build fully qualified mailbox names.
A server may return multiple namespace descriptors per category, or NIL if no namespaces of that type exist. This class preserves all namespace descriptors exactly as returned by the server.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_Namespace.#ctor(LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Namespace_Entry[],LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Namespace_Entry[],LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Namespace_Entry[])
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class using the personal, other‑users, and shared namespace lists returned by the IMAP server.
member.param: The list of personal namespace entries. This corresponds to the first namespace list in the IMAP NAMESPACE response and describes the mailbox hierarchy belonging to the authenticated user. Must not be null.

The list of other‑users namespace entries. This corresponds to the second namespace list in the IMAP NAMESPACE response and describes mailbox hierarchies belonging to other users that may be accessible depending on server permissions. Must not be null.

The list of shared namespace entries. This corresponds to the third namespace list in the IMAP NAMESPACE response and describes mailbox hierarchies that are accessible to multiple users, such as public folders or shared mailbox trees. Must not be null.
member.exception: Thrown when any of the provided namespace lists is null.

Optional cancellation token used when reading prefix, delimiter, or extension values that may be encoded as literals.
member.returns: A fully parsed instance containing the personal, other-users, and shared namespace lists.

Thrown if the NAMESPACE response is syntactically invalid, contains an illegal delimiter, includes NIL where an astring is required, or violates RFC 2342 structural rules.

member.summary: Returns the IMAP NAMESPACE response string representing the personal, other‑users, and shared namespaces contained in this instance.

A properly formatted IMAP NAMESPACE response line ending with CRLF. The output follows the syntax defined in RFC 2342 and includes three namespace lists in the form:
* NAMESPACE (personal) (other-users) (shared)
Each namespace list is either:
A parenthesized list of namespace descriptors, where each descriptor has the form ("prefix" "delimiter").
NIL, indicating that no namespaces of that type exist.

If the server returns NIL for the personal namespace list, this property contains an empty array.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_Quota
member.summary: Represents an IMAP untagged QUOTA response as defined in RFC 2087. A QUOTA response reports the current usage and maximum allowed usage for one or more quota resources within a specific quota root.

remarks.para: The QUOTA response has the following general syntax:
remarks.code: * QUOTA <quotaroot> (<resource> <usage> <limit> ...)
remarks.para: The quotaroot identifies the resource domain for which quota information is being reported. It is an IMAP astring and may be an atom or a quoted string.
Each resource triplet consists of:
remarks.code: <resource> <usage> <limit>
remarks.para: Resource names are case‑insensitive atoms such as STORAGE or MESSAGE. The usage field specifies the current consumption of the resource (kilobytes for STORAGE, message count for MESSAGE). The limit field specifies the maximum allowed usage using the same units.
This class provides strongly‑typed access to the quota root and the collection of resource entries, as well as serialization back into the IMAP QUOTA response format.

QUOTA responses have the general form:
remarks.code: * QUOTA <quotaroot> (<resource> <usage> <limit> ...)
remarks.para: The quotaroot value in this property is the first field following the QUOTA keyword and uniquely identifies the quota domain for all resource entries contained in the response.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_QuotaRoot
member.summary: Represents an IMAP untagged QUOTAROOT response as defined in RFC 2087. A QUOTAROOT response reports the quota roots associated with a specific mailbox, allowing the client to determine which quota domains apply to that mailbox.

remarks.para: The QUOTAROOT response has the following general syntax:
remarks.code: * QUOTAROOT <mailbox> <root1> [<root2> ...]
remarks.para: The first argument is the mailbox name for which quota information is being queried.

Following the mailbox are one or more quota roots. A quota root identifies a resource domain for which the server tracks usage and limits. A mailbox may belong to multiple quota roots, and the server may return them in any order.

The QUOTAROOT response does not itself contain usage or limit values. Those values are returned separately in QUOTA responses. Clients typically issue a GETQUOTAROOT command, receive a QUOTAROOT response listing the applicable roots, and then receive one or more QUOTA responses providing the actual resource usage for each root.

The array of quota root names associated with the mailbox. Each root identifies a resource domain for which usage and limit values may be reported in subsequent QUOTA responses. The array must not be null. Servers may legally return zero quota roots.

Thrown when is an empty string, as a mailbox name must be specified.

remarks.para: A QUOTAROOT response reports the quota roots that apply to a mailbox. It does not contain usage or limit values; those are returned separately in QUOTA responses. Unknown or server‑specific quota roots are preserved for forward compatibility.
The general response format is:
remarks.code: * QUOTAROOT <mailbox> <root1> [<root2> ...]

The general response format is:
remarks.code: * QUOTAROOT <mailbox> <root1> [<root2> ...]

Each root is an IMAP astring and may be an atom or a quoted string. All values are decoded from IMAP UTF‑7 before being stored.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_Recent
member.summary: Represents the IMAP RECENT untagged server status response as defined in RFC 3501 section 7.3.2.
member.remarks:
The RECENT response reports the number of messages in the selected mailbox that have the \Recent flag set. This response is sent during a SELECT or EXAMINE command and may also appear whenever the mailbox size changes (for example, when new messages arrive).
The RECENT count does not necessarily correspond to a contiguous range of the newest messages. Multiple concurrent sessions or external mailbox reordering can cause non‑contiguous recent message numbering. The only reliable way to identify recent messages is by checking the \Recent flag on individual messages or performing a SEARCH RECENT.
Clients MUST record updates from the RECENT response.

The RECENT response reports the number of messages in the selected mailbox that have the \Recent flag set. This response is sent during SELECT or EXAMINE and may also appear when the mailbox size changes (e.g., new messages arriving).
The RECENT count does not necessarily correspond to the newest messages or a contiguous range. Multiple concurrent sessions or external mailbox reordering can cause non‑contiguous recent message numbering.

remarks.para: A SEARCH response is always untagged and consists of the literal *, followed by the atom SEARCH, followed by zero or more integers. No other data items appear in a SEARCH response.

item.description: For SEARCH, the integers are message sequence numbers.
For UID SEARCH, the integers are UIDs.

remarks.para: If no messages match the criteria, the server sends: * SEARCH with no numbers following it.
This class stores the returned identifiers exactly as provided by the server. Interpretation (sequence number vs. UID) is determined by the caller based on the command used.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_ServerStatus
member.summary:
Represents an untagged IMAP status response (* OK, * NO, * BAD, * PREAUTH, * BYE) as defined in RFC 3501 section 7.1.
Untagged status responses are sent by the server outside the context of a specific client command and always begin with the asterisk (*) tag. They may include an optional response code enclosed in square brackets (e.g. [UIDNEXT 123]), followed by free-form human‑readable text. Status responses never contain IMAP literals; any braces or brackets appearing in the response text are treated as plain characters.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_ServerStatus.#ctor(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Initializes a new untagged IMAP status response with the specified response code and response text. This overload creates a status response without an optional response code, corresponding to lines such as * OK Completed.
member.param: The IMAP status response code (OK, NO, BAD, PREAUTH, or BYE).
The free-form human-readable text that follows the status code. Status responses never contain IMAP literals; any braces or brackets appearing in the text are treated as plain characters.

member.summary:
Initializes a new untagged IMAP status response with the specified response code, optional response code, and response text. Untagged status responses always begin with the asterisk (*) tag and correspond to server‑generated status lines such as * OK, * NO, * BAD, * PREAUTH, or * BYE.
If present, the optional response code is the bracketed element defined in RFC 3501 section 7.1.2 (for example [UIDNEXT 123]). Only one optional response code may appear in a status response. The remaining text is free‑form human‑readable response text. Status responses never contain IMAP literals; any braces or brackets appearing in the text are treated as plain characters.
member.param: The IMAP status response code (OK, NO, BAD, PREAUTH, or BYE).
The optional bracketed response code (e.g. [UIDNEXT 123]), or null if no optional response code is present.
The free‑form text that follows the status code. This text never contains IMAP literals and may be empty.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_ServerStatus.Parse(System.String)
member.summary:
Parses an untagged IMAP status response from a single response line. Untagged status responses begin with the asterisk (*) tag and use the same syntax as tagged status responses, except that the tag is always fixed.
This method parses:
The mandatory untagged response marker (*).
The mandatory IMAP status response code (OK, NO, BAD, PREAUTH, or BYE), as defined in RFC 3501 section 7.1.
An optional response code enclosed in square brackets (e.g. [UIDNEXT 123]), as defined in RFC 3501 section 7.1.2. Only one optional response code may appear.
The free-form response text that follows the status code. Status responses never contain IMAP literals; any braces or brackets appearing in the text are treated as plain characters.
member.param: The raw IMAP response line received from the server.
member.returns: An instance representing the parsed untagged IMAP status response.
member.exception: Thrown when is null.
Thrown when the response line violates IMAP syntax, such as missing the untagged marker (*), missing a response code, or containing a malformed optional response code.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_ServerStatus.ToString
member.summary: Returns the IMAP wire-format representation of this untagged status response. The returned string always begins with the untagged marker (*) followed by the status response code (OK, NO, BAD, PREAUTH, or BYE). If present, the optional response code is emitted inside square brackets (e.g. [UIDNEXT 123]) exactly as defined in RFC 3501 section 7.1.2. The remainder of the line is the free-form response text, followed by CRLF.
member.returns: A CRLF-terminated IMAP status response line suitable for transmission to an IMAP client. Status responses never contain IMAP literals; any braces or brackets in the response text are emitted verbatim.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_Status
member.summary: Represents an untagged IMAP STATUS response as defined by RFC 9051. A STATUS response provides selected metadata about a mailbox without requiring the client to SELECT or EXAMINE it.

remarks.para: The IMAP STATUS command allows a client to request specific mailbox metadata items without changing the currently selected mailbox. The client sends a command of the form:
remarks.code: A01 STATUS mailbox-name (MESSAGES UIDNEXT UNSEEN)
remarks.para: The server replies with an untagged STATUS response containing the requested status data items:
remarks.code: * STATUS mailbox-name (MESSAGES 231 UIDNEXT 44292 UNSEEN 8)
remarks.para: All STATUS data items are optional. Each item is represented in this class using nullable values so that null indicates that the corresponding item was not present in the server response.
IMAP4rev2 defines the following STATUS data items:

item.description: MESSAGES - Total number of messages in the mailbox.
UIDNEXT - Next UID to be assigned.
UIDVALIDITY - UID validity value of the mailbox.
UNSEEN - Number of messages without the \Seen flag.
DELETED - Number of messages with the \Deleted flag.
SIZE - Total size, in bytes, of all messages in the mailbox.

remarks.para: For compatibility with IMAP4rev1 servers, the obsolete RECENT status data item may also be present.
This class derives from , the base type for all untagged IMAP responses.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_Status.#ctor(System.String,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Nullable{System.Int64},System.Nullable{System.Int64},System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Nullable{System.Int64},System.Nullable{System.Int32})
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class using the mailbox name and the optional STATUS data items returned by the IMAP server.
member.param: The mailbox name associated with this STATUS response.
The total number of messages in the mailbox (MESSAGES), or null if the server did not include this item.
The next unique identifier (UID) that will be assigned to a new message in the mailbox (UIDNEXT), or null if omitted by the server.
The UID validity value of the mailbox (UIDVALIDITY). May be null if the server did not include this item.
The number of messages that do not have the \Seen flag set (UNSEEN), or null if omitted by the server.
The number of messages that have the \Deleted flag set (DELETED), or null if omitted by the server.
The total size, in bytes, of all messages in the mailbox (SIZE), or null if omitted by the server.
The number of messages that have the \Recent flag set (RECENT), or null if the server did not include this item.
member.exception: Thrown when is null.
Thrown when is an empty string.

remarks.para: All STATUS data items are optional. IMAP servers include only the items explicitly requested by the client. Nullable parameters reflect this behavior directly.

The DELETED and SIZE status data items were introduced by IMAP4rev2 (RFC 9051). The RECENT status data item is obsolete in IMAP4rev2 but may still be returned by servers for compatibility with IMAP4rev1 clients.

The output format follows RFC 9051:

IMAP mailbox names do not include hierarchy delimiters or attribute flags; those are provided separately in LIST/LSUB responses.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_Status.MessagesCount
member.summary: Gets the total number of messages in the mailbox (MESSAGES), or null if the server did not include this item in the STATUS response.

remarks.para: The MESSAGES data item represents the total number of messages currently stored in the mailbox. It is one of the optional fields that may appear in an IMAP STATUS response (RFC 3501 section 7.2.4).
IMAP servers include only the STATUS items explicitly requested by the client. When the server omits MESSAGES, this property will be null.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_Status.UidNext
member.summary: Gets the next unique identifier (UID) that the IMAP server will assign to the next message delivered to the mailbox (UIDNEXT), or null if the server did not include this item in the STATUS response.

remarks.para: The UIDNEXT data item represents the UID that will be assigned to the next message added to the mailbox. It is one of the optional fields that may appear in an IMAP STATUS response (RFC 3501 section 7.2.4).
IMAP servers include only the STATUS items explicitly requested by the client. When the server omits UIDNEXT, this property will be null.

UIDNEXT does not indicate whether a new message has already arrived. It only specifies the UID that will be used for the next message added. The value increases monotonically for the lifetime of the mailbox.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_Status.FolderUidValidity
member.summary: Gets the UID validity value of the mailbox (UIDVALIDITY), or null if the server did not include this item in the STATUS response.

remarks.para: The UIDVALIDITY data item is a monotonically increasing value assigned by the IMAP server to indicate the stability of the mailbox’s UID sequence. When the mailbox is recreated or its UID sequence becomes invalid, the server assigns a new UIDVALIDITY value.
Clients use UIDVALIDITY to determine whether previously cached UIDs remain valid. If the UIDVALIDITY value changes, all cached UIDs for the mailbox must be discarded.
UIDVALIDITY is optional in a STATUS response. IMAP servers include only the items explicitly requested by the client. When omitted, this property will be null.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_Status.UnseenCount
member.summary: Gets the number of messages in the mailbox that do not have the \Seen flag set (UNSEEN), or null if the server did not include this item in the STATUS response.

remarks.para: The UNSEEN data item represents the count of messages that the server considers unread. It is one of the optional fields that may appear in an IMAP STATUS response (RFC 3501 section 7.2.4).
IMAP servers include only the STATUS items explicitly requested by the client. When the server omits UNSEEN, this property will be null.
Unlike RECENT, which indicates newly delivered messages since the last mailbox open, UNSEEN reflects the current number of messages lacking the \Seen flag, regardless of when they arrived.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_Status.DeletedCount
member.summary: Gets the number of messages in the mailbox that have the \Deleted flag set (DELETED), or null if the server did not include this item in the STATUS response.

remarks.para: The DELETED status data item represents the number of messages currently marked with the \Deleted flag in the mailbox.
The DELETED status data item was introduced by IMAP4rev2 (RFC 9051).
IMAP servers include only the STATUS items explicitly requested by the client. When the server omits DELETED, this property will be null.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_Status.Size
member.summary: Gets the total size, in bytes, of all messages in the mailbox (SIZE), or null if the server did not include this item in the STATUS response.

remarks.para: The SIZE status data item represents the total size, in bytes, of all messages contained in the mailbox.
The SIZE status data item was introduced by IMAP4rev2 (RFC 9051).
IMAP servers include only the STATUS items explicitly requested by the client. When the server omits SIZE, this property will be null.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_r_u_Status.RecentCount
member.summary: Gets the number of messages in the mailbox that have the \Recent flag set (RECENT), or null if the server did not include this item in the STATUS response.

remarks.para: The RECENT status data item represents the number of messages that have the \Recent flag set in the mailbox. This status item was defined by IMAP4rev1 (RFC 3501) and may still be returned by servers for compatibility with older clients.
The RECENT status data item and the \Recent flag are obsolete in IMAP4rev2 (RFC 9051).
IMAP servers include only the STATUS items explicitly requested by the client. When the server omits RECENT, this property will be null.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_BodyStructure_e
member.summary: Defines the abstract base type for IMAP BODYSTRUCTURE elements returned by the IMAP FETCH BODYSTRUCTURE command.
member.remarks:
A BODYSTRUCTURE element describes the MIME structure of a message part according to RFC 3501 section 7.4.2. Concrete implementations represent either single‑part entities (such as text/plain, image/jpeg, or message/rfc822) or multipart entities (such as multipart/mixed, multipart/alternative, or multipart/related).
The base class exposes common MIME metadata fields including , , , and . Derived classes provide the structural details required by the IMAP grammar, such as multipart child parts or single‑part size and encoding information.

member.summary: Represents an IMAP BODYSTRUCTURE multipart entity as defined in RFC 3501 section 7.4.2.
member.remarks: A multipart body structure contains one or more child BODYSTRUCTURE elements, each of which may be either a single‑part or another multipart structure. member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_BodyStructure_e_MultiPart.ParseAsync(LumiSoft.Net.IMAP._IMAP_Reader,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Parses an IMAP BODYSTRUCTURE multipart element according to RFC 3501 section 7.4.2.
member.param: The IMAP reader positioned at the opening parenthesis of the multipart container.
A cancellation token that can be used to cancel the asynchronous operation.
member.returns:
A populated instance containing:
One or more child BODYSTRUCTURE elements.
The multipart subtype (e.g., mixed, alternative, related).
Optional extension fields: disposition, language, and location.
member.exception: Thrown when the multipart syntax is invalid, the subtype is missing or NIL, or any structural element does not conform to RFC 3501.
member.remarks: The method distinguishes multipart from single‑part structures by examining the raw character stream: multipart containers always begin with (( because the first child BODYSTRUCTURE immediately follows the multipart's opening parenthesis. Child elements are parsed recursively until a non‑parenthesis token indicates the multipart subtype.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Fetch_i
member.summary:
Base class for all IMAP FETCH request data‑items as defined in RFC 3501 section 6.4.5. Each derived type represents a specific attribute that may be included in a FETCH command, such as BODY, BODY.PEEK, FLAGS, UID, or Gmail‑specific extensions like X-GM-LABELS, X-GM-THRID, and X-GM-MSGID.
FETCH data‑items instruct the server which message attributes or content fragments to return. They may request metadata, message flags, envelope information, body structure, or specific body sections with optional partial‑fetch parameters.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Fetch_i_Body
member.summary:
Represents the IMAP BODY FETCH request data‑item as defined in RFC 3501 section 6.4.5 and section 7.4.2. When included in a FETCH command, this attribute instructs the server to return the specified message body section.
The client may specify:
A body section (e.g., 1, 2.1, HEADER, TEXT, MIME)
An optional partial fetch using an offset and optional maximum byte count
A null section requests the entire message body.
Semantics: BODY returns the requested message body section. Unlike BODY.PEEK, retrieving a body section using BODY may cause the server to set the \Seen flag on the message, depending on server implementation. Partial fetches return a substring beginning at the specified byte offset. The server echoes only the offset in the response; the literal size indicates how many bytes were actually returned.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Fetch_i_Body.#ctor
member.summary:
Initializes a new instance with no section and no partial‑fetch parameters specified.
This corresponds to the IMAP BODY[] FETCH data‑item, which requests the entire message body. No offset or length is included, so the server returns the complete content of the message body section.
Semantics: Unlike BODY.PEEK, retrieving a body section using BODY may cause the server to set the \Seen flag on the message, depending on server implementation.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Fetch_i_Body.#ctor(System.String,System.Nullable{System.Int64},System.Nullable{System.Int64})
member.summary:
Initializes a new instance with an optional section name and optional partial‑fetch parameters.
This constructor models the IMAP BODY FETCH data‑item as defined in RFC 3501 section 6.4.5 and section 7.4.2. The parameters correspond to the syntax:
BODY[section]<offset[.length]>

Represents the IMAP INTERNALDATE FETCH request data‑item as defined in RFC 3501 section 7.4.2. When included in a FETCH command, this attribute instructs the server to return the message's internal creation timestamp.
Semantics: The INTERNALDATE attribute returns the server‑assigned timestamp indicating when the message was added to the mailbox. This value is distinct from the message's RFC822 Date: header field and is always returned as an IMAP date‑time string in the format:

Represents the IMAP UID FETCH request data‑item as defined in RFC 3501 section 6.4.5. When included in a FETCH command, the UID data‑item instructs the server to return the unique identifier assigned to each matching message.
Semantics: The UID data‑item is a FETCH attribute that causes the server to return the message's UID in the corresponding FETCH response. member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Fetch_i_xGmailLabels
member.summary:
Represents the Gmail‑specific X-GM-LABELS FETCH request data‑item as defined in the Gmail IMAP Extensions documentation. When included in a FETCH command, this attribute instructs the server to return the full set of Gmail labels assigned to the message.
Gmail labels may include:
System labels such as \Inbox, \Important, \Starred, \Draft
User‑defined labels such as Work, ProjectA, Invoices
Labels are returned as a parenthesized list of quoted strings.
Semantics: X-GM-LABELS exposes Gmail’s label model, which differs from traditional IMAP folders. A message may have multiple labels simultaneously, and labels do not imply physical storage locations. This data‑item is informational only and does not modify message flags.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Fetch_i_xGmailMsgId
member.summary:
Represents the Gmail‑specific X-GM-MSGID FETCH request data‑item as defined in the Gmail IMAP Extensions documentation. When included in a FETCH command, this attribute instructs the server to return the stable 64‑bit immutable message identifier assigned internally by Gmail.
Unlike IMAP UIDs, which may change when messages are moved, when UIDVALIDITY changes, or when folders are rebuilt, the X-GM-MSGID value remains constant for the lifetime of the message. The identifier is returned as a decimal 64‑bit integer.
Semantics: X-GM-MSGID provides a persistent, cross‑folder message identifier suitable for:
Deduplication
Cross‑folder correlation
Stable message tracking across sync cycles
Conversation analysis (when paired with X-GM-THRID)
The value is informational only and does not modify message flags or server state.

Stable thread tracking across sync cycles

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Fetch_r_i_Body
member.summary: Represents a BODY data-item used in IMAP FETCH results.

remarks.para: This object models the content associated with a BODY FETCH element as defined in RFC 3501. It provides access to the section identifier, optional starting offset, and the stream containing the raw octets of the referenced message portion.

The section identifier corresponds to the text inside the square brackets of a BODY[section] specification. An empty string indicates that no section was specified, meaning the data-item refers to the complete message content associated with BODY[].

The offset value indicates the byte position at which the returned data begins. A value of -1 signifies that no explicit offset was provided. When no offset is specified, the section is interpreted as beginning at position zero.
The stream contains the exact literal bytes associated with the section and offset. No decoding, transformation, or interpretation is applied to the content stored in the stream.

The INTERNALDATE attribute is defined in RFC 3501 section 7.4.2 as the server‑stored internal creation timestamp of a message. It appears in FETCH responses in the form:

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Fetch_r_i_xGmailLabels
member.summary:
Represents the Gmail‑specific IMAP extension data item X-GM-LABELS returned within a FETCH response. Gmail exposes all labels assigned to a message as a parenthesized list of IMAP strings, where each string corresponds to either a system label (such as \Inbox or \Important) or a user‑defined label.
Labels are Gmail’s organizational model and a single message may have zero, one, or many labels simultaneously. The values stored in this object are the raw UTF‑8 label strings exactly as transmitted by Gmail, without normalization, mapping, or client‑side interpretation.
X-GM-LABELS is part of Gmail’s proprietary IMAP extensions and is not defined by RFC 3501. Servers other than Gmail do not return this data item.

The values supplied to this constructor are the raw UTF‑8 label strings exactly as parsed from the server response, without normalization or client‑side mapping.
The array must not be null. An empty array indicates that the message has no labels assigned.

Represents the Gmail‑specific IMAP extension data item X-GM-MSGID returned within a FETCH response. Gmail assigns each message a stable 64‑bit identifier that remains constant for the lifetime of the message, regardless of label changes, mailbox movement, UID renumbering, or UIDVALIDITY changes.
X-GM-MSGID is part of Gmail’s proprietary IMAP extensions and is not defined by RFC 3501. The identifier is transmitted as a decimal 64‑bit integer. Although Gmail defines the value as unsigned, all known values fit within the positive range of a signed , which is used for consistency with other IMAP numeric fields such as UID, UIDVALIDITY, and UIDNEXT.
The value exposed by this class is suitable for stable message tracking, deduplication, cross‑folder correlation, and threading (when paired with the X-GM-THRID extension).

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Namespace_Entry
member.summary: Represents a single namespace descriptor returned in an IMAP NAMESPACE response as defined in RFC 2342. A namespace entry consists of a prefix and an optional hierarchy delimiter and describes one logical mailbox namespace advertised by the server.

remarks.para: Each namespace entry has the form:
remarks.code: (<prefix> <delimiter>)
remarks.para: The prefix identifies the logical root of the namespace. It may be an empty string ("") or any server-defined value such as "INBOX.", "Public/", or "#shared". Prefixes may be quoted strings in the raw NAMESPACE response and may contain vendor-specific or implementation-specific values. This implementation preserves the prefix exactly as parsed.

The delimiter specifies the hierarchy separator used within the namespace. Common values are '/' or '.'. If the delimiter is null, the server has returned NIL, indicating that the namespace is flat and has no hierarchical structure. In this case, mailbox names MUST NOT be combined using a separator, and the prefix is applied directly without inserting any delimiter.

Namespace entries appear inside the untagged NAMESPACE response, which contains three lists: personal namespaces, other-users namespaces, and shared namespaces. Servers may return multiple entries per category.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Namespace_Entry.#ctor(System.String,System.Nullable{System.Char})
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class using the specified namespace prefix and hierarchy delimiter.
member.param: The namespace prefix as returned by the server. The prefix identifies the logical root of the namespace and may be an empty string ("") or any server‑defined value such as "INBOX.", "Public/", or "#shared". The value must not be null.

The hierarchy delimiter for this namespace. Common values are '/' or '.'. If the value is null, the server has returned NIL, indicating that the namespace is flat and has no hierarchical structure. In this case, mailbox names MUST NOT be combined using a separator, and the prefix is applied directly without inserting any delimiter.
member.exception: Thrown when is null.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Namespace_Entry.Prefix
member.summary: Gets the namespace prefix associated with this namespace entry. The prefix identifies the logical root under which the server exposes mailboxes belonging to this namespace.

remarks.para: Namespace prefixes are defined in RFC 2342 (IMAP4 Namespace Extension). A prefix is an IMAP string that specifies the base path for a mailbox namespace. It may be an empty string (""), meaning the root of the hierarchy, or any server‑defined value such as "INBOX.", "Public/", or "#shared".

Prefixes may be quoted strings in the raw NAMESPACE response and may contain vendor‑specific or implementation‑specific values. This implementation preserves the prefix exactly as parsed so that clients can construct mailbox names correctly and without assumptions.

When combined with the namespace delimiter (if one exists), the prefix forms the base path used to construct fully qualified mailbox names. If the delimiter is NIL, the namespace is flat and the prefix is applied without inserting a hierarchy separator.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Namespace_Entry.Delimiter
member.summary: Gets the hierarchy delimiter associated with this namespace entry. The delimiter defines how child mailbox names are combined with the namespace prefix when constructing fully qualified mailbox paths.

remarks.para: Namespace delimiters are defined in RFC 2342 (IMAP4 Namespace Extension). A delimiter is normally a single character such as '/' or '.' and indicates the hierarchy separator used within the namespace. For example, a prefix of "INBOX." with a delimiter of '.' produces mailbox names such as "INBOX.Work".

If the delimiter is null, the server has returned NIL for the delimiter field, meaning that the namespace is flat and has no hierarchical structure. In this case, mailbox names MUST NOT be combined using a separator, and the prefix is applied directly without inserting any delimiter. For example, a prefix of "#shared" with a null delimiter yields mailbox names such as "#sharedReports" rather than "#shared/Reports".
Delimiters are preserved exactly as parsed. Unknown or vendor‑specific delimiter characters are allowed, although null is the only non‑character value permitted by RFC 2342.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Quota_Entry
member.summary: Represents a single quota resource entry in an IMAP QUOTA response, as defined in RFC 2087. Each entry reports the current usage and the maximum allowed usage for a specific quota resource within a quota root.

remarks.para: A quota entry corresponds to one resource triplet in the QUOTA response:
remarks.code: <resource> <usage> <limit>
remarks.para: The resource field identifies the quota resource being tracked. Common resource names include STORAGE (kilobytes of space used) and MESSAGE (number of messages), but servers may define additional resource types. Resource names are case‑insensitive IMAP atoms and are preserved exactly as provided by the server.

The usage field specifies the current consumption of the resource. For STORAGE, usage is measured in kilobytes; for MESSAGE, usage is the number of messages. The limit field specifies the maximum allowed usage for the resource, using the same units as usage.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Quota_Entry.#ctor(System.String,System.Int64,System.Int64)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class using the specified resource name, usage value, and limit value.
member.param: The name of the quota resource being reported (for example, STORAGE or MESSAGE). Resource names are case‑insensitive IMAP atoms and must be a non‑empty string.
The current usage of the resource, as defined in RFC 2087. For STORAGE, usage is measured in kilobytes; for MESSAGE, usage is the number of messages.
The maximum allowed usage for the resource. The interpretation matches the resource type: kilobytes for STORAGE, message count for MESSAGE. The limit is always an integer.
member.exception: Thrown when is null.
Thrown when is an empty string.

remarks.para: A quota entry represents one resource triplet in a QUOTA response:
remarks.code: <resource> <usage> <limit>

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Quota_Entry.ResourceName
member.summary: Gets the name of the quota resource reported in this QUOTA entry.

remarks.para: A quota resource identifies the type of usage being tracked for a quota root, as defined in RFC 2087. Common resource names include STORAGE (kilobytes of space used) and MESSAGE (number of messages stored), but servers may define additional resource types.
Resource names are case‑insensitive IMAP atoms and are returned exactly as provided by the server. The parser preserves unknown or non‑standard resource names for forward compatibility.
Each QUOTA entry consists of:
remarks.code: <resource> <usage> <limit>
remarks.para: where resource is this property, usage is the current usage value, and limit is the maximum allowed usage for the resource.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Quota_Entry.Usage
member.summary: Gets the current usage value for this quota resource, as reported by the server in the QUOTA response.

remarks.para: The usage value represents the amount of the resource currently consumed within the quota root, as defined in RFC 2087. The interpretation of the value depends on the resource type:

member.summary: Represents the IMAP ALL search key, which selects every message in the currently selected mailbox.

remarks.para: The ALL search key is defined by RFC 9051 as the most permissive search criterion. When used in a SEARCH or UID SEARCH command, it instructs the server to return all messages without applying any additional filtering.

This search key is commonly used as a baseline criterion or as part of compound search expressions. For example, clients may combine ALL with other search keys to ensure predictable behavior when constructing complex queries.

member.summary: Represents the IMAP HEADER search key, which selects messages whose specified header field contains the given value.

remarks.para: The HEADER search key is defined by RFC 9051. If the value string is zero-length, the search matches all messages that contain the specified header field-name, regardless of the header’s contents.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.IMAP_t_Search_Key_New
member.summary: Represents the IMAP NEW search key, which matches messages that are both \Recent and not marked with \Seen.

remarks.para: The NEW search key is defined by RFC 3501 as a composite search criterion equivalent to RECENT UNSEEN. It selects messages that have been newly delivered to the mailbox and have not yet been read.

This search key is obsolete in IMAP4rev2 (RFC 9051) because the \Recent message flag has been removed from the protocol. New applications should use other search criteria and should not rely on the presence of the NEW search key.
Support for this search key is retained only for compatibility with IMAP4rev1 clients.

member.summary: Returns the IMAP NEW search key.
member.returns: The string NEW, which matches messages that are both \Recent and not marked with \Seen.
member.remarks: The NEW search key is defined by RFC 3501 as a convenience composite: it selects messages that are newly delivered to the mailbox (\Recent) and have not yet been read (\Seen not set). Like other flag‑type search keys, it carries no associated value and is serialized as a fixed keyword in IMAP SEARCH and UID SEARCH commands.

remarks.para: The NEW search key is defined by RFC 3501 as a composite search criterion equivalent to RECENT NOT SEEN. It matches messages that are newly delivered to the mailbox and have not yet been read.
Although NEW is conceptually composite, it is serialized as the literal keyword NEW in IMAP SEARCH and UID SEARCH commands.

This event allows an application to supply message data for IMAP FETCH requests.
The IMAP session determines which information is required to satisfy the FETCH request and exposes the requirements through the , , and properties.
Event handlers should call for each message that is to be included in the FETCH response.
A handler may supply:
The complete RFC 5322 message stream.
A parsed instance.
A parsed instance.
Envelope and body structure information may be returned from application caches to avoid reparsing the message stream for every FETCH operation.
Some FETCH requests require the fetched messages to be marked with the \Seen flag. This requirement is exposed through the property. When the property is , the event handler is responsible for persisting the corresponding flag update in the message store.

The version value is used by the IMAP session to determine whether the mailbox state has changed since the previous synchronization.
The value must change whenever mailbox state changes in a way that may affect IMAP clients, such as message additions, removals, or flag updates.
The format of the version is implementation-specific. The IMAP session compares version values for equality and does not interpret their contents.

The value is used by the IMAP session to determine whether the mailbox state has changed since the last synchronization.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Server.IMAP_Session._SelectedFolder.MaxUid
member.summary: Gets the highest UID ever observed by the selected mailbox cache.
member.remarks:
This value is used to validate mailbox synchronization data and detect newly added messages.
A newly discovered message that does not already exist in the session cache is generally expected to have a UID greater than this value.
Unlike sequence numbers, IMAP UIDs are monotonically increasing. Consequently, this value is not reduced when messages are removed from the mailbox.

member.summary:
Is raised when an IMAP session processes an UNSUBSCRIBE command and requires removal of a mailbox subscription. Event handlers must examine the provided instance and set an appropriate response indicating whether the request was processed successfully or why it failed.
In accordance with RFC 9051, a successful response should also be returned when the specified mailbox is not currently subscribed.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Server.IMAP_Session.StatusAsync
member.summary: Is raised when an IMAP session processes a STATUS command and requires mailbox status information. Event handlers must examine the provided instance, populate the available status data items, and set an appropriate response indicating whether the request was processed successfully or why it failed.
member.remarks: IMAP servers include only the STATUS data items explicitly requested by the client. The server is responsible for selecting which populated values are returned in the STATUS response.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Server.IMAP_Session.SelectAsync
member.summary: Is raised when an IMAP session processes a SELECT command and requires mailbox information. Event handlers must examine the provided instance, populate , and set an appropriate response indicating whether the mailbox was selected successfully or why the request failed.
member.remarks: Event handlers should populate with metadata for all messages currently contained in the mailbox. The server caches this information and uses it to service subsequent mailbox operations such as FETCH, STORE, SEARCH, COPY, EXPUNGE, and sequence number to UID mapping.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Server.IMAP_Session.ExamineAsync
member.summary: Is raised when an IMAP session processes an EXAMINE command and requires mailbox information. Event handlers must examine the provided instance, populate , and set an appropriate response indicating whether the mailbox was opened successfully in read-only mode or why the request failed.
member.remarks:
Event handlers should populate with metadata for all messages currently contained in the mailbox. The server caches this information and uses it to service subsequent mailbox operations such as FETCH, SEARCH, and sequence number to UID mapping.
A successful response should normally contain a response code.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Server.IMAP_Session.FolderSyncAsync
member.summary: Is raised when the IMAP session synchronizes the state of the selected mailbox.
member.remarks:
This event allows an application to determine whether the mailbox has changed since the previous synchronization and, if necessary, supply the current mailbox state.
The mailbox version known to the IMAP session is available through the property.
If the current mailbox version differs from , the event handler should set to the current mailbox version and provide the complete mailbox UID set through .
Message information supplied through may contain either the complete mailbox snapshot or only messages that have been added or modified since the previous synchronization.
The IMAP session uses the supplied information to detect message additions, removals, and flag changes and generates the appropriate mailbox update responses.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Server.IMAP_Session.AppendBeginAsync
member.summary: Is raised when an IMAP session processes an APPEND command and before the message literal is read from the client. Event handlers may validate the operation, reject the APPEND request by setting , or provide a writable destination stream through into which the incoming message will be stored.
member.remarks: This event is intended for mailbox validation, permission checks, quota checks, and allocation of message storage before any message data is received from the client.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Server.IMAP_Session.AppendCancelAsync
member.summary: Is raised when an APPEND operation is cancelled and the message cannot be stored successfully.
member.remarks:
Typical causes include:
Client connection closed during literal transfer.
Session timeout.
I/O or storage failure.
Unexpected processing error.
This event allows applications to perform cleanup of temporary files, streams, or other resources associated with the failed APPEND operation.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Server.IMAP_Session.AppendCompleteAsync
member.summary: Is raised when an APPEND message literal has been successfully received from the client and written to the destination stream. Event handlers may finalize message storage, update mailbox metadata, and set the final response that will be returned to the client.
member.remarks: Event handlers should set an appropriate OK or NO response. For successful APPEND operations, servers supporting the UIDPLUS extension (RFC 4315) should include an optional response code in the returned OK response.
