member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Server.IMAP_Session.FetchAsync
member.summary: Is raised when an IMAP session processes a FETCH command and requires the application to supply message data.
member.remarks:
The messages included in the FETCH operation are available through the property.
The IMAP session determines which information is required to satisfy the FETCH request and exposes the requirements through the , , and properties.
Event handlers should call
for each message that is to be included in the FETCH response.
A handler may provide:
The complete RFC 5322 message stream.
A parsed instance.
A parsed instance.
Envelope and body structure data may be supplied from an application cache, avoiding the need to parse them from the message stream for each FETCH operation.
If is , the event handler must persist the corresponding \Seen flag update for the fetched messages.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Server.IMAP_Session.SearchAsync
member.summary: Is raised when an IMAP session processes a SEARCH command and requires the application to evaluate search criteria that cannot be satisfied using the selected mailbox cache alone.
member.remarks:
The parsed SEARCH expression is available through the property.
Event handlers should populate the property with the UIDs of all messages matching the supplied search criteria.
The IMAP server automatically converts returned UIDs to message sequence numbers when processing a SEARCH command. For UID SEARCH commands, the returned UIDs are sent directly to the client.
Event handlers must assign an appropriate response indicating whether the search operation completed successfully or why it failed.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Server.IMAP_Session.StoreAsync
member.summary: Is raised when an IMAP session processes a STORE command and requires one or more message flags to be updated. Event handlers must examine the provided instance and set an appropriate response indicating whether the operation completed successfully or why it failed.
member.remarks:
The property contains the messages affected by the operation.
The property specifies whether the supplied flags replace, add to, or remove existing message flags.
The flags supplied by the client are available through the property.
When a successful response is returned, the IMAP server updates the cached mailbox state and automatically generates any required FETCH responses associated with the STORE operation.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP.Server.IMAP_Session.CopyAsync
member.summary: Is raised when an IMAP session processes a COPY command and requires one or more messages to be copied from a source mailbox to a destination mailbox. Event handlers must examine the provided instance and set an appropriate response indicating whether the copy operation completed successfully or why it failed.
member.remarks:
The original sequence set supplied by the client is available through the property.
The property indicates whether the operation originated from a COPY or UID COPY command.
The property contains the messages resolved from the supplied sequence set. Each contains the application's internal message identifier together with the cached IMAP message metadata for the current session.
For servers supporting the UIDPLUS extension (RFC 4315), successful copy operations should include an optional response code in the returned OK response.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP._IMAP_Reader
member.summary:
Provides low-level parsing utilities for IMAP tokens such as atoms, quoted strings, literals, astrings, mailbox names, and other grammar elements defined by IMAP4rev2.
The reader operates on a single IMAP protocol line supplied by the caller and exposes methods for extracting individual tokens according to IMAP grammar rules.
The class does not perform general protocol-line reading. All parsing is performed within the current protocol line except when a literal is encountered. In that case, the reader reads the literal payload from the underlying and then loads the next protocol line so that parsing may continue. This is the only situation in which the reader performs stream I/O.
Supported literal forms include standard literals ({N}), non-synchronizing literals ({N+}), literal8 (~{N}), and UTF8 literals (UTF8 (~{N})).
The reader supports both client and server operation. When running in server mode, the reader automatically sends IMAP continuation responses ("+ Continue") for synchronizing literals. In client mode, continuation responses are never sent.
The class is intended for internal use by higher-level IMAP command and response parsers. It provides deterministic, grammar-aware token extraction without altering the caller's parsing state except when literal processing requires advancing to the next protocol line.

A literal header describes an IMAP literal without reading its payload. Supported forms include standard literals ({N}), non-synchronizing literals ({N+}), literal8 (~{N}), and UTF8 literals (UTF8 (~{N})).

member.summary:
Reads an IMAP mailbox name using and applies mailbox-specific decoding rules.
A mailbox name in IMAP is represented as an astring and may therefore be encoded as an atom, a quoted string, a literal, a literal8 value, a UTF8 literal, or the special token NIL.
If the mailbox name is represented by NIL, the method returns null.
For non-null values, the mailbox name is decoded using . This preserves compatibility with mailbox names encoded using IMAP modified UTF-7 while also allowing UTF-8 mailbox names when supported by the server.

member.summary:
Skips any whitespace at the current reader position and returns the next character, advancing m_Position by one. This method performs a consuming read and is used when parsing IMAP tokens that require sequential character processing such as atoms, quoted strings, section specifiers, and other grammar elements.
Whitespace characters (SP, HTAB, CR, LF) are skipped using before the character is returned. If the end of the line is reached, the method returns '\0'.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP._IMAP_Reader.ReadParenthesized
member.summary:
Reads an IMAP parenthesized list of the form ( ... ) from the current protocol line. Parenthesized lists are used throughout IMAP4rev1 grammar for constructs such as FLAGS, ENVELOPE, BODYSTRUCTURE, and various nested attribute lists.
The method first skips leading whitespace and then verifies that the next character is an opening parenthesis. It consumes the entire balanced parenthesized block, including any nested parentheses, and returns the raw inner content without the surrounding ( and ) delimiters.
This method does not interpret the returned content. Callers are responsible for further tokenizing the inner list (for example splitting flag atoms, parsing ENVELOPE fields, or recursively processing BODYSTRUCTURE elements).
member.returns: The substring contained within the balanced parenthesized block, excluding the outer parentheses.
member.exception: Thrown if the next non‑whitespace character is not '(', or if the parenthesized block is not properly balanced before the end of the line.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP._IMAP_Reader.ReadBracketed
member.summary: Reads a bracketed value of the form [ ... ] from the current position in the input stream.

remarks.para: The method consumes the opening bracket, reads all characters until the matching closing bracket, and returns the inner content without the surrounding [ and ] delimiters.

member.returns: The text contained inside the bracket pair, or an empty string if no bracketed value is present.
member.exception: Thrown if the next non‑whitespace character is not '[', or if the parenthesized block is not properly balanced before the end of the line.

Reads a literal payload from the underlying connection and returns it as a byte array.
The literal header is parsed from the current protocol line and used to determine the literal size, synchronization mode, and literal type. Supported forms include standard literals ({N}), non-synchronizing literals ({N+}), literal8 (~{N}), and UTF8 literals (UTF8 (~{N})).
After the literal payload has been read, the next protocol line becomes the current parsing line. For UTF8 literals, the closing parenthesis terminating the UTF8 literal wrapper is consumed automatically.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP._IMAP_Reader.PeekChar
member.summary:
Returns the next character in the current IMAP protocol line without advancing the reader position. This method provides lightweight look‑ahead functionality used by higher‑level parsing routines to determine the type of the upcoming token (for example quoted strings, literals, atoms, or the special token NIL).
If the reader position is already at or beyond the end of the current line, the method returns the null character ('\0') to indicate that no further characters are available. This allows callers to safely test for end‑of‑line conditions without throwing exceptions or performing additional bounds checks.
PeekChar() does not interpret or classify the returned character; it simply exposes the raw protocol character so that the caller can decide how to proceed. Typical use cases include checking for the opening quote of a quoted string, the opening brace of a literal header, or whitespace that should be skipped before parsing an atom.
member.returns: The next character in the current protocol line, or '\0' if the reader position is at or beyond the end of the line.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP._IMAP_Reader.PeekIs(System.Char)
member.summary:
Determines whether the next non‑whitespace character in the current IMAP protocol line equals the specified character. This method performs a pure look‑ahead operation: whitespace characters (SP, HTAB, CR, LF) are skipped using a temporary index so that m_Position remains unchanged.
This method is typically used to detect structural delimiters such as the closing parenthesis in FETCH responses or other IMAP grammar boundaries without consuming any input.
member.param: The character to compare against the next non‑whitespace character.
member.returns: true if the next non‑whitespace character equals ; otherwise false.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP._IMAP_Reader.PeekIs(System.String)
member.summary:
Determines whether the next non‑whitespace characters in the current IMAP protocol line match the specified token, using a case‑insensitive comparison, without advancing or modifying the reader position.
The method performs a pure look‑ahead check. Leading whitespace characters (SP, HTAB, CR, LF) are skipped using a temporary index so that keyword detection is not affected by spacing, but the actual reader position (m_Position) remains unchanged. This allows callers to inspect the upcoming token safely without consuming any input or altering subsequent parsing behavior.
The comparison is performed using , since IMAP keywords such as NIL, BODY, FETCH, and ENVELOPE are case‑insensitive. If is null, or if the token is longer than the remaining characters in the line after whitespace skipping, the method returns false.
member.param: The token to compare against the upcoming non‑whitespace characters in the current protocol line. The comparison is case‑insensitive. If null, the method returns false.
member.returns: true if the next non‑whitespace characters match using a case‑insensitive comparison; otherwise false.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.IMAP._IMAP_Reader.PeekIsLiteral
member.summary:
Determines whether the next non-whitespace token is an IMAP literal construct without consuming any input or modifying the current reader position.
This method performs a lightweight look-ahead operation and recognizes all literal forms supported by the reader, including standard literals ({N}), non-synchronizing literals ({N+}), literal8 (~{N}), and UTF8 literals (UTF8 (~{N})).
No literal payload data is read and no network or stream I/O is performed. The method only inspects the current protocol line.
The method is intended for parser logic that needs to determine whether the next token requires literal processing before deciding how to read the value.
member.returns: true if the next non-whitespace token is a valid IMAP literal construct; otherwise false.

This property provides a lightweight end‑of‑line check that can be used by higher‑level parsers to determine whether further tokens may be read without attempting to consume input or inspect the underlying stream.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.Mail.Mail_h_Received
member.summary: Represents a Received header field.
member.remarks:
Defined by RFC 5321, section 4.4. A received field records the hosts, protocols, and timestamp associated with an SMTP hop.
RFC 5321 4.4. Time-stamp-line = "Received:" FWS Stamp CRLF
Stamp = From-domain By-domain Opt-info [CFWS] ";" FWS date-time ; where "date-time" is as defined in RFC 5322 [4] ; but the "obs-" forms, especially two-digit ; years, are prohibited in SMTP and MUST NOT be used.
From-domain = "FROM" FWS Extended-Domain
By-domain = CFWS "BY" FWS Extended-Domain
Extended-Domain = Domain / ( Domain FWS "(" TCP-info ")" ) / ( address-literal FWS "(" TCP-info ")" )
TCP-info = address-literal / ( Domain FWS address-literal ) ; Information derived by server from TCP connection not client EHLO.
Opt-info = [Via] [With] [ID] [For] [Additional-Registered-Clauses]
Via = CFWS "VIA" FWS Link
With = CFWS "WITH" FWS Protocol
ID = CFWS "ID" FWS ( Atom / msg-id ) ; msg-id is defined in RFC 5322 [4]
For = CFWS "FOR" FWS ( Path / Mailbox )
Additional-Registered-Clauses = CFWS Atom FWS String
Link = "TCP" / Addtl-Link
Addtl-Link = Atom
Protocol = "ESMTP" / "SMTP" / Attdl-Protocol
Mailbox = Local-part "@" ( Domain / address-literal )

member.summary: This class represents WAVEFORMATEX structure.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media.AudioIn.WaveIn.WAVEFORMATEX.wFormatTag
member.summary: Waveform-audio format type. Format tags are registered with Microsoft Corporation for many compression algorithms. A complete list of format tags can be found in the Mmreg.h header file. For one- or two-channel PCM data, this value should be WAVE_FORMAT_PCM. When this structure is included in a WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE structure, this value must be WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media.AudioIn.WaveIn.WAVEFORMATEX.nChannels
member.summary: Number of channels in the waveform-audio data. Monaural data uses one channel and stereo data uses two channels.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media.AudioIn.WaveIn.WAVEFORMATEX.nSamplesPerSec
member.summary: Sample rate, in samples per second (hertz). If wFormatTag is WAVE_FORMAT_PCM, then common values for nSamplesPerSec are 8.0 kHz, 11.025 kHz, 22.05 kHz, and 44.1 kHz.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media.AudioIn.WaveIn.WAVEFORMATEX.nAvgBytesPerSec
member.summary: Required average data-transfer rate, in bytes per second, for the format tag. If wFormatTag is WAVE_FORMAT_PCM, nAvgBytesPerSec should be equal to the product of nSamplesPerSec and nBlockAlign.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media.AudioIn.WaveIn.WAVEFORMATEX.nBlockAlign
member.summary: Block alignment, in bytes. The block alignment is the minimum atomic unit of data for the wFormatTag format type. If wFormatTag is WAVE_FORMAT_PCM or WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE, nBlockAlign must be equal to the product of nChannels and wBitsPerSample divided by 8 (bits per byte).

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media.AudioIn.WaveIn.WAVEFORMATEX.wBitsPerSample
member.summary: Bits per sample for the wFormatTag format type. If wFormatTag is WAVE_FORMAT_PCM, then wBitsPerSample should be equal to 8 or 16.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media.AudioIn.WaveIn.WAVEFORMATEX.cbSize
member.summary: Size, in bytes, of extra format information appended to the end of the WAVEFORMATEX structure.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.Media.AudioOut.WaveOut.WAVEFORMATEX
member.summary: This class represents WAVEFORMATEX structure.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media.AudioOut.WaveOut.WAVEFORMATEX.wFormatTag
member.summary: Waveform-audio format type. Format tags are registered with Microsoft Corporation for many compression algorithms. A complete list of format tags can be found in the Mmreg.h header file. For one- or two-channel PCM data, this value should be WAVE_FORMAT_PCM. When this structure is included in a WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE structure, this value must be WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media.AudioOut.WaveOut.WAVEFORMATEX.nChannels
member.summary: Number of channels in the waveform-audio data. Monaural data uses one channel and stereo data uses two channels.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media.AudioOut.WaveOut.WAVEFORMATEX.nSamplesPerSec
member.summary: Sample rate, in samples per second (hertz). If wFormatTag is WAVE_FORMAT_PCM, then common values for nSamplesPerSec are 8.0 kHz, 11.025 kHz, 22.05 kHz, and 44.1 kHz.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media.AudioOut.WaveOut.WAVEFORMATEX.nAvgBytesPerSec
member.summary: Required average data-transfer rate, in bytes per second, for the format tag. If wFormatTag is WAVE_FORMAT_PCM, nAvgBytesPerSec should be equal to the product of nSamplesPerSec and nBlockAlign.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media.AudioOut.WaveOut.WAVEFORMATEX.nBlockAlign
member.summary: Block alignment, in bytes. The block alignment is the minimum atomic unit of data for the wFormatTag format type. If wFormatTag is WAVE_FORMAT_PCM or WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE, nBlockAlign must be equal to the product of nChannels and wBitsPerSample divided by 8 (bits per byte).

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media.AudioOut.WaveOut.WAVEFORMATEX.wBitsPerSample
member.summary: Bits per sample for the wFormatTag format type. If wFormatTag is WAVE_FORMAT_PCM, then wBitsPerSample should be equal to 8 or 16.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media.AudioOut.WaveOut.WAVEFORMATEX.cbSize
member.summary: Size, in bytes, of extra format information appended to the end of the WAVEFORMATEX structure.

member.summary: The waveInOpen function opens the given waveform-audio input device for recording.
member.param: Pointer to a buffer that receives a handle identifying the open waveform-audio input device.

Identifier of the waveform-audio input device to open. It can be either a device identifier or a handle of an open waveform-audio input device. You can use the following flag instead of a device identifier.
Pointer to a WAVEFORMATEX structure that identifies the desired format for recording waveform-audio data. You can free this structure immediately after waveInOpen returns.

Pointer to a fixed callback function, an event handle, a handle to a window, or the identifier of a thread to be called during waveform-audio recording to process messages related to the progress of recording. If no callback function is required, this value can be zero. For more information on the callback function, see waveInProc.
User-instance data passed to the callback mechanism.
Flags for opening the device.

member.summary: This class represents WAVEFORMATEX structure.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media._WaveIn.WAVEFORMATEX.wFormatTag
member.summary: Waveform-audio format type. Format tags are registered with Microsoft Corporation for many compression algorithms. A complete list of format tags can be found in the Mmreg.h header file. For one- or two-channel PCM data, this value should be WAVE_FORMAT_PCM. When this structure is included in a WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE structure, this value must be WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media._WaveIn.WAVEFORMATEX.nChannels
member.summary: Number of channels in the waveform-audio data. Monaural data uses one channel and stereo data uses two channels.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media._WaveIn.WAVEFORMATEX.nSamplesPerSec
member.summary: Sample rate, in samples per second (hertz). If wFormatTag is WAVE_FORMAT_PCM, then common values for nSamplesPerSec are 8.0 kHz, 11.025 kHz, 22.05 kHz, and 44.1 kHz.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media._WaveIn.WAVEFORMATEX.nAvgBytesPerSec
member.summary: Required average data-transfer rate, in bytes per second, for the format tag. If wFormatTag is WAVE_FORMAT_PCM, nAvgBytesPerSec should be equal to the product of nSamplesPerSec and nBlockAlign.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media._WaveIn.WAVEFORMATEX.nBlockAlign
member.summary: Block alignment, in bytes. The block alignment is the minimum atomic unit of data for the wFormatTag format type. If wFormatTag is WAVE_FORMAT_PCM or WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE, nBlockAlign must be equal to the product of nChannels and wBitsPerSample divided by 8 (bits per byte).

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media._WaveIn.WAVEFORMATEX.wBitsPerSample
member.summary: Bits per sample for the wFormatTag format type. If wFormatTag is WAVE_FORMAT_PCM, then wBitsPerSample should be equal to 8 or 16.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.Media._WaveIn.WAVEFORMATEX.cbSize
member.summary: Size, in bytes, of extra format information appended to the end of the WAVEFORMATEX structure.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.MIME.MIME_b_MessageDeliveryStatus
member.summary: Represents a MIME message/delivery-status body as defined in RFC 3464.
member.remarks:
A message/delivery-status body contains delivery status notification (DSN) fields describing the delivery status of a message. It consists of a per-message field block followed by one or more per-recipient field blocks.
delivery-status-content = per-message-fields 1*( CRLF per-recipient-fields )
per-message-fields = [ original-envelope-id-field CRLF ] reporting-mta-field CRLF [ dsn-gateway-field CRLF ] [ received-from-mta-field CRLF ] [ arrival-date-field CRLF ] *( extension-field CRLF )
per-recipient-fields = [ original-recipient-field CRLF ] final-recipient-field CRLF action-field CRLF status-field CRLF [ remote-mta-field CRLF ] [ diagnostic-code-field CRLF ] [ last-attempt-date-field CRLF ] [ final-log-id-field CRLF ] [ will-retry-until-field CRLF ] *( extension-field CRLF )

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.MIME.MIME_Entity.ReadHeaderAsync(System.IO.Stream,System.Int64,System.Boolean,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
Asynchronously reads and extracts MIME headers from the stream up to the standard \r\n\r\n terminator, enforcing a strict maximum size limit to protect against memory exhaustion attacks.
This method uses an efficient vectorized sliding window with a 3-byte overlap to reliably detect terminators even if they span across buffer read boundaries. Upon completion, the underlying stream's position is automatically repositioned precisely at the start of the body payload.
member.param: The source stream positioned at the start of the MIME entity.
The maximum allowed size of the header block in bytes (e.g., 1,048,576 for 1 MB).
If true, reaching the end of the stream without finding a \r\n\r\n terminator will treat all accumulated content as headers and assume an empty body rather than throwing an exception.
A token to monitor for cancellation requests.
member.returns: A string containing the raw ASCII header block.
member.exception: Thrown if is null.
Thrown if the headers exceed the threshold, or if the end of the stream is reached before finding the \r\n\r\n terminator (when is false).

modification-date-parm := "modification-date" "=" quoted-date-time
read-date-parm := "read-date" "=" quoted-date-time

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.POP3.Client.POP3_Client
member.summary: Implements a POP3 client as defined in RFC 1939, RFC 2449 (CAPA), and RFC 2595 (STLS). The class provides high‑level methods for connecting to a POP3 server, negotiating optional TLS, authenticating, retrieving server capabilities, and performing POP3 operations such as listing, retrieving, and deleting messages.

remarks.para: A POP3 session consists of three protocol states:

item.description: AUTHORIZATION – The client connects to the server and receives the greeting. Authentication is performed using USER/PASS, APOP, or SASL (when supported).

TRANSACTION – After successful authentication, the client may issue commands such as LIST, UIDL, RETR, TOP, DELE, and NOOP. The message list may be loaded using or , but this is optional. The client can be used without ever loading the message list.
UPDATE – Entered when the client sends QUIT. The server applies any pending deletions and closes the connection.

remarks.para: TLS negotiation is supported via the POP3 STLS command (RFC 2595). When TLS is enabled, all subsequent commands are transmitted over the secure channel.
Server capabilities are retrieved using the CAPA command (RFC 2449). The client automatically detects support for extensions such as UIDL, UTF8, and UTF8=USER.

The property exposes cached message metadata (size and optional unique‑id) after the message list has been loaded. Accessing this property is optional; callers may instead use LIST, UIDL, RETR, and TOP directly.
All network operations are available in both synchronous and asynchronous forms. The synchronous wrappers apply the configured value to limit operation duration.

member.summary: Default constructor.

member.summary: Clean up any resources being used.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.POP3.Client.POP3_Client.OnConnectedAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Handles the POP3 server greeting received immediately after the TCP connection is established. According to RFC 1939 section 6, the server sends a single greeting line beginning with +OK, optionally followed by a unique APOP challenge and human‑readable text.
member.param: A token that may be used to cancel the asynchronous read operation.
member.returns: A representing the asynchronous operation.
member.exception: Thrown when the POP3 server returns a negative greeting (-ERR).

remarks.para: POP3 greeting syntax (RFC 1939 §6):
remarks.code: Greeting = "+OK" [ SP greeting-text ] CRLF greeting-text = [ unique-id ] [ SP human-text ] unique-id = "<" *CHAR ">" ; Required for APOP authentication
remarks.para: If a unique-id is present, it MUST be the first token in greeting-text. The unique-id is extracted and stored for optional APOP authentication. Any remaining text is stored as the server's human-readable greeting.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.POP3.Client.POP3_Client.Disconnect
member.summary: Disconnects from the POP3 server by invoking the asynchronous method with sendQuit set to true and waiting for its completion.

remarks.para: This synchronous wrapper uses the configured value to create a that limits the duration of the disconnect sequence. The underlying asynchronous method sends the POP3 QUIT command, reads the server's final response, clears all session state, and closes the connection.
Any exceptions raised during the asynchronous disconnect sequence are propagated to the caller.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.POP3.Client.POP3_Client.DisconnectAsync(System.Boolean,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Disconnects from the POP3 server and optionally sends the QUIT command before closing the connection.
member.param: If true, the method sends the POP3 QUIT command and reads the server's final response before terminating the connection.
A token that may be used to cancel the asynchronous write or read operations performed during the disconnect sequence.
member.returns: A representing the asynchronous disconnect operation.
member.exception: Thrown when the client instance has already been disposed.
Thrown when the client is not currently connected.

remarks.para: When is true, the method attempts to send the POP3 QUIT command and read the server's final reply. Any exceptions raised during this exchange are suppressed, and the connection is closed regardless.
All POP3 session state (greeting text, APOP unique-id, capability list, message cache, and authenticated identity) is cleared before the underlying connection is closed.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.POP3.Client.POP3_Client.Capa
member.summary: Retrieves the POP3 capability list by invoking the asynchronous method and waiting for its completion. This synchronous wrapper uses the configured value to limit the duration of the operation.
member.returns: A instance containing the server's initial +OK or -ERR response to the CAPA command.
member.exception: Thrown when the client instance has already been disposed.
Thrown when the client is not currently connected.
Thrown when the server returns malformed data or violates POP3 protocol rules.

remarks.para: The underlying asynchronous method sends the POP3 CAPA command, reads the server's initial status response, and if successful, reads the multiline capability list terminated by a single dot (.). All capability lines are stored in the client's internal capability collection.
Any exceptions raised during the asynchronous capability retrieval are propagated to the caller of this method.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.POP3.Client.POP3_Client.CapaAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Sends the POP3 CAPA command to the server and retrieves the capability list defined in RFC 2449. The method clears any previously cached capabilities, issues the command, reads the server's initial status response, and if successful, reads the multiline capability list terminated by a single dot (.).
member.param: A token that may be used to cancel the asynchronous write or read operations performed while retrieving the capability list.
member.returns: A instance containing the server's initial +OK or -ERR response to the CAPA command.
member.exception: Thrown when the client instance has already been disposed.
Thrown when the client is not currently connected.
Thrown when the server returns a negative (-ERR) response to the CAPA command.
Thrown when the POP3 server closes the connection before the capability list is fully read.
Thrown when the server returns malformed data or violates POP3 protocol rules.

remarks.para: The POP3 CAPA command (RFC 2449) returns a list of server capabilities, one per line, optionally followed by parameters. The list is terminated by a line containing only a dot (.).
A negative (-ERR) response indicates that the server does not implement the CAPA command, and the client must fall back to probing for individual capabilities.
The method stores each capability line verbatim in the internal capability collection.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.POP3.Client.POP3_Client.Stls(System.Net.Security.SslClientAuthenticationOptions)
member.summary: Sends the POP3 STLS command and, if accepted by the server, upgrades the existing plaintext connection to a secure TLS connection by invoking the asynchronous method and waiting for its completion.
member.param:
Optional TLS configuration. If null, a permissive legacy‑compatible configuration is applied inside:
TLS 1.2 only
Certificate revocation checking disabled
Renegotiation allowed
ALPN disabled
No client certificates
Certificate validation callback that accepts all certificates
These defaults maximize compatibility with older servers.
member.returns: A instance containing the server's initial +OK or -ERR response to the STLS command.
member.exception: Thrown when the client instance has already been disposed.
Thrown when the client is not connected, when the connection is already secure, or when the STLS command is issued after authentication.
Thrown when the server returns a negative (-ERR) response to the STLS command.
Thrown when the TLS negotiation fails after the server accepts STLS.

remarks.para: This synchronous wrapper uses the configured value to create a that limits the duration of the STLS negotiation. The underlying asynchronous method sends the STLS command, reads the server's response, and if successful, performs the TLS negotiation.

remarks.code: + <base64-challenge>

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.POP3.Client.POP3_ClientMessage
member.summary: Represents a single POP3 message within an active POP3 session.

remarks.para: Instances of are created internally by when processing the POP3 LIST and UIDL commands. Each instance corresponds to a single message stored on the POP3 server and exposes convenience methods for retrieving message metadata, headers, partial content, full content, and for marking the message for deletion.

POP3 message numbers are 1‑based and valid only for the duration of the current POP3 session, as defined in RFC 1939. The message size and unique identifier (UID) are obtained from the POP3 LIST and UIDL commands respectively. The UID is stable across sessions when supported by the server.
This class provides both synchronous and asynchronous methods for:

item.description: Retrieving message headers using the POP3 TOP command.
Retrieving partial message content using a byte limit.
Retrieving full message content using the POP3 RETR command.
Parsing retrieved data into a MIME object.
Marking the message for deletion using the POP3 DELE command.

remarks.para: Header‑only and partial‑body retrieval methods are useful for lightweight message inspection, such as reading Subject, From, Date, or other metadata without downloading the full message body.

A message marked for deletion remains accessible for the duration of the session. The POP3 server performs the actual deletion only when the session ends with QUIT, entering the UPDATE state as defined in RFC 1939.
All synchronous methods in this class internally wrap their asynchronous counterparts and use the POP3 client's configured timeout to ensure consistent blocking behavior across the API.
Instances of this class are not thread‑safe. Concurrent access should be coordinated externally if required.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.POP3.Server.POP3_e_GetMessageStream
member.summary:
Provides event data for the GetMessageStreamAsync POP3 server event. A instance is created when the server requires a readable RFC‑822 message stream for a specific message, typically during handling of the RETR or TOP commands.
The property identifies the server‑side message descriptor, while the event handler is responsible for assigning a readable stream to . The POP3 server will consume the stream according to command semantics: RETR reads the entire message, whereas TOP reads headers and a limited number of body lines.
If the message does not exist or cannot be opened, the handler must leave set to null. In this case the server will return an appropriate -ERR response to the client.

member.summary:
Initializes a new instance for the specified POP3 session and message. This event‑args object is used when the server requires a readable RFC‑822 message stream, typically in response to RETR or TOP commands.
The session identifies the active POP3 transaction, while the instance provides the metadata needed to locate and open the message content. The event handler is expected to supply a stream containing the full message; the POP3 server will read from the stream according to command semantics.
member.param: The POP3 session for which the message stream is being requested. This value must not be null.
The server‑side message descriptor identifying the message whose content should be streamed. This value must not be null.
member.exception: Thrown when or is null.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.POP3.Server.POP3_e_GetMessageStream.Session
member.summary: Gets the POP3 session associated with this event. The session provides access to connection state, authentication status, and server-side context required to process the current POP3 command.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.POP3.Server.POP3_e_GetMessageStream.Message
member.summary:
Gets the instance that describes the message for which a stream is being requested. This object contains the server‑side metadata associated with the message, such as its sequence number, size, and storage reference.
The POP3 server uses this descriptor to locate and open the underlying RFC‑822 message content when handling RETR or TOP commands. The event handler assigned to GetMessageStreamAsync is expected to use this metadata to provide a readable stream containing the full message.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.POP3.Server.POP3_e_GetMessageStream.MessageStream
member.summary:
Gets or sets the stream that provides the RFC‑822 message content for the requested POP3 message. The event handler assigned to GetMessageStreamAsync should supply a readable stream containing the full message (headers followed by body) when the message exists.
If the message does not exist or cannot be opened, the handler must leave this property set to null. In that case the POP3 server will return an appropriate -ERR response to the client.
The stream must contain the message in canonical CRLF format. The POP3 server performs dot‑stuffing and multi‑line termination when sending data to the client. The server will dispose the stream once message transmission is complete.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.POP3.Server.POP3_Session.LoadMessagesInfoAsync
member.summary: Raised after successful USER/PASS or AUTH authentication when the server needs to retrieve message metadata (sizes and UIDLs) for the authenticated POP3 session. Handlers must populate the message list so the server can enter the TRANSACTION state and serve STAT,LIST, UIDL, RETR, TOP and DELE commands.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.POP3.Server.POP3_Session.GetMessageStreamAsync
member.summary:
Event that is raised when the POP3 server needs to obtain a readable message stream for a specific message. This event is used by both the RETR and TOP commands, allowing the server to expose a single retrieval mechanism regardless of how much of the message the client intends to read.
The event handler must provide a stream containing the full RFC‑822 message (headers followed by body). The POP3 server will read from the returned stream according to the command semantics:
RETR — the server reads the entire stream and sends the complete message to the client.
TOP — the server reads headers and the requested number of body lines, then stops reading.
The handler is responsible for opening the stream and ensuring it remains readable for the duration of the operation. The server will dispose the stream when message transmission is complete.
member.remarks: Implementations may return any readable including file streams, memory streams, or custom streaming sources. The stream must contain the message in canonical CRLF format and must not perform dot‑stuffing; the POP3 server applies dot‑stuffing when sending data to the client.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.POP3.Server.POP3_Session.DeleteMessagesAsync
member.summary: Raised when the POP3 session ends with a successful QUIT command and the server requires the host application to delete all messages that were marked for deletion during the TRANSACTION state.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_OptionTags
member.summary: SIP Option Tags. Defined in RFC 3261 27.1, defined values are in: http://www.iana.org/assignments/sip-parameters.
member.remarks: Option tags are used in header fields such as Require, Supported, Proxy-Require, and Unsupported in support of SIP compatibility mechanisms for extensions (Section 19.2). The option tag itself is a string that is associated with a particular SIP option (that is, an extension).

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_OptionTags.x100rel
member.summary: This option tag is for reliability of provisional responses. When present in a Supported header, it indicates that the UA can send or receive reliable provisional responses. When present in a Require header in a request it indicates that the UAS MUST send all provisional responses reliably. When present in a Require header in a reliable provisional response, it indicates that the response is to be sent reliably. Defined in rfc 3262.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_OptionTags.early_session
member.summary: A UA adding the early-session option tag to a message indicates that it understands the early-session content disposition. Defined in rfc 3959.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_OptionTags.eventlist
member.summary: Extension to allow subscriptions to lists of resources. Defined in rfc 4662.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_OptionTags.histinfo
member.summary: When used with the Supported header, this option tag indicates support for the History Information to be captured for requests and returned in subsequent responses. This tag is not used in a Proxy-Require or Require header field since support of History-Info is optional. Defined in rfc 4244.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_OptionTags.join
member.summary: Support for the SIP Join Header. Defined in rfc 3911.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_OptionTags.norefersub
member.summary: This option tag specifies a User Agent ability of accepting a REFER request without establishing an implicit subscription (compared to the default case defined in RFC3515). Defined in rfc 3911.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_OptionTags.path
member.summary: A SIP UA that supports the Path extension header field includes this option tag as a header field value in a Supported header field in all requests generated by that UA. Intermediate proxies may use the presence of this option tag in a REGISTER request to determine whether to offer Path service for for that request. If an intermediate proxy requires that the registrar support Path for a request, then it includes this option tag as a header field value in a Requires header field in that request. Defined in rfc 3327.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_OptionTags.precondition
member.summary: An offerer MUST include this tag in the Require header field if the offer contains one or more "mandatory" strength-tags. If all the strength-tags in the description are "optional" or "none" the offerer MUST include this tag either in a Supported header field or in a Require header field. Defined in rfc 3312.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_OptionTags.pref
member.summary: This option tag is used to ensure that a server understands the callee capabilities parameters used in the request. Defined in rfc 3840.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_OptionTags.privacy
member.summary: This option tag indicates support for the Privacy mechanism. When used in the Proxy-Require header, it indicates that proxy servers do not forward the request unless they can provide the requested privacy service. This tag is not used in the Require or Supported headers. Proxies remove this option tag before forwarding the request if the desired privacy function has been performed. Defined in rfc 3323.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_OptionTags.replaces
member.summary: This option tag indicates support for the SIP Replaces header. Defined in rfc 3891.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_OptionTags.resource_priority
member.summary: Indicates or requests support for the resource priority mechanism. Defined in rfc 4412.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_OptionTags.sdp_anat
member.summary: The option-tag sdp-anat is defined for use in the Require and Supported SIP [RFC3261] header fields. SIP user agents that place this option-tag in a Supported header field understand the ANAT semantics as defined in [RFC4091]. Defined in rfc 4092.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_OptionTags.sec_agree
member.summary: This option tag indicates support for the Security Agreement mechanism. When used in the Require, or Proxy-Require headers, it indicates that proxy servers are required to use the Security Agreement mechanism. When used in the Supported header, it indicates that the User Agent Client supports the Security Agreement mechanism. When used in the Require header in the 494 (Security Agreement Required) or 421 (Extension Required) responses, it indicates that the User Agent Client must use the Security Agreement Mechanism. Defined in rfc 3329.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_OptionTags.tdialog
member.summary: This option tag is used to identify the target dialog header field extension. When used in a Require header field, it implies that the recipient needs to support the Target-Dialog header field. When used in a Supported header field, it implies that the sender of the message supports it. Defined in rfc 4538.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_OptionTags.timer
member.summary: This option tag is for support of the session timer extension. Inclusion in a Supported header field in a request or response indicates that the UA is capable of performing refreshes according to that specification. Inclusion in a Require header in a request means that the UAS must understand the session timer extension to process the request. Inclusion in a Require header field in a response indicates that the UAC must look for the Session-Expires header field in the response, and process accordingly. Defined in rfc 4028.

member.summary: Implements SIP "directive" value. Defined in RFC 3841.

remarks.code: RFC 3841 Syntax: directive = proxy-directive / cancel-directive / fork-directive / recurse-directive / parallel-directive / queue-directive proxy-directive = "proxy" / "redirect" cancel-directive = "cancel" / "no-cancel" fork-directive = "fork" / "no-fork" recurse-directive = "recurse" / "no-recurse" parallel-directive = "parallel" / "sequential" queue-directive = "queue" / "no-queue"

member.summary: Proccess directives. Defined in rfc 3841 9.1.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_Directive.DirectiveType.Proxy
member.summary: This directive indicates whether the caller would like each server to proxy request.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_Directive.DirectiveType.Redirect
member.summary: This directive indicates whether the caller would like each server to redirect request.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_Directive.DirectiveType.Cancel
member.summary: This directive indicates whether the caller would like each proxy server to send a CANCEL request to forked branches.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_Directive.DirectiveType.NoCancel
member.summary: This directive indicates whether the caller would NOT want each proxy server to send a CANCEL request to forked branches.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_Directive.DirectiveType.Fork
member.summary: This type of directive indicates whether a proxy should fork a request.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_Directive.DirectiveType.NoFork
member.summary: This type of directive indicates whether a proxy should proxy to only a single address. The server SHOULD proxy the request to the "best" address (generally the one with the highest q-value).

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_Directive.DirectiveType.Recurse
member.summary: This directive indicates whether a proxy server receiving a 3xx response should send requests to the addresses listed in the response.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_Directive.DirectiveType.NoRecurse
member.summary: This directive indicates whether a proxy server receiving a 3xx response should forward the list of addresses upstream towards the caller.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_Directive.DirectiveType.Parallel
member.summary: This directive indicates whether the caller would like the proxy server to proxy the request to all known addresses at once.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_Directive.DirectiveType.Sequential
member.summary: This directive indicates whether the caller would like the proxy server to go through all known addresses sequentially, contacting the next address only after it has received a non-2xx or non-6xx final response for the previous one.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_Directive.DirectiveType.Queue
member.summary: This directive indicates whether if the called party is temporarily unreachable, caller wants to have its call queued.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_Directive.DirectiveType.NoQueue
member.summary: This directive indicates whether if the called party is temporarily unreachable, caller don't want its call to be queued.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_SubscriptionState
member.summary: Implements SIP "Subscription-State" value. Defined in RFC 3265.

remarks.code: RFC 3265 Syntax: Subscription-State = substate-value *( SEMI subexp-params ) substate-value = "active" / "pending" / "terminated" / extension-substate extension-substate = token subexp-params = ("reason" EQUAL event-reason-value) / ("expires" EQUAL delta-seconds) / ("retry-after" EQUAL delta-seconds) / generic-param event-reason-value = "deactivated" / "probation" / "rejected" / "timeout" / "giveup" / "noresource" / event-reason-extension event-reason-extension = token

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_SubscriptionState.SubscriptionState
member.summary: This class holds 'substate-value' values.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_SubscriptionState.SubscriptionState.active
member.summary: The subscription has been accepted and (in general) has been authorized.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_SubscriptionState.SubscriptionState.pending
member.summary: The subscription has been received by the notifier, but there is insufficient policy information to grant or deny the subscription yet.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_SubscriptionState.SubscriptionState.terminated
member.summary: The subscriber should consider the subscription terminated.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_SubscriptionState.EventReason
member.summary: This class holds 'event-reason-value' values.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_SubscriptionState.EventReason.deactivated
member.summary: The subscription has been terminated, but the subscriber SHOULD retry immediately with a new subscription. One primary use of such a status code is to allow migration of subscriptions between nodes. The "retry-after" parameter has no semantics for "deactivated".

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_SubscriptionState.EventReason.probation
member.summary: The subscription has been terminated, but the client SHOULD retry at some later time. If a "retry-after" parameter is also present, the client SHOULD wait at least the number of seconds specified by that parameter before attempting to re-subscribe.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_SubscriptionState.EventReason.rejected
member.summary: The subscription has been terminated due to change in authorization policy. Clients SHOULD NOT attempt to re-subscribe. The "retry-after" parameter has no semantics for "rejected".

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_SubscriptionState.EventReason.timeout
member.summary: The subscription has been terminated because it was not refreshed before it expired. Clients MAY re-subscribe immediately. The "retry-after" parameter has no semantics for "timeout".

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_SubscriptionState.EventReason.giveup
member.summary: The subscription has been terminated because the notifier could not obtain authorization in a timely fashion. If a "retry-after" parameter is also present, the client SHOULD wait at least the number of seconds specified by that parameter before attempting to re-subscribe; otherwise, the client MAY retry immediately, but will likely get put back into pending state.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_SubscriptionState.EventReason.noresource
member.summary: The subscription has been terminated because the resource state which was being monitored no longer exists. Clients SHOULD NOT attempt to re-subscribe. The "retry-after" parameter has no semantics for "noresource".

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Message.SIP_t_ViaParm
member.summary: Implements SIP "via-parm" value. Defined in RFC 3261.

remarks.code:
RFC 3261 Syntax: via-parm = sent-protocol LWS sent-by *( SEMI via-params ) via-params = via-ttl / via-maddr / via-received / via-branch / via-extension via-ttl = "ttl" EQUAL ttl via-maddr = "maddr" EQUAL host via-received = "received" EQUAL (IPv4address / IPv6address) via-branch = "branch" EQUAL token via-extension = generic-param sent-protocol = protocol-name SLASH protocol-version SLASH transport protocol-name = "SIP" / token protocol-version = token transport = "UDP" / "TCP" / "TLS" / "SCTP" / other-transport sent-by = host [ COLON port ] ttl = 1*3DIGIT ; 0 to 255
Via extentions: // RFC 3486 via-compression = "comp" EQUAL ("sigcomp" / other-compression) // RFC 3581 response-port = "rport" [EQUAL 1*DIGIT]

member.remarks: A Flow is a network protocol layer (layer 4) association between two hosts that is represented by the network address and port number of both ends and by the protocol. For TCP, a flow is equivalent to a TCP connection. For UDP a flow is a bidirectional stream of datagrams between a single pair of IP addresses and ports of both peers.

member.summary: This response indicates that the request has been received by the next-hop server and that some unspecified action is being taken on behalf of this call (for example, a database is being consulted).

member.summary: The UA receiving the INVITE is trying to alert the user.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x181_Call_Forwarded
member.summary: A server MAY use this status code to indicate that the call is being forwarded to a different set of destinations.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x182_Queued
member.summary: The called party is temporarily unavailable, but the server has decided to queue the call rather than reject it. When the callee becomes available, it will return the appropriate final status response.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x183_Session_Progress
member.summary: The 183 (Session Progress) response is used to convey information about the progress of the call that is not otherwise classified.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x200_Ok
member.summary: The request has succeeded.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x202_Ok
member.summary: The request has accepted. Defined in rfc 3265.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x301_Ok
member.summary: The user can no longer be found at the address in the Request-URI, and the requesting client SHOULD retry at the new address given by the Contact header field (Section 20.10). Defined in rfc 3265.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x302_Ok
member.summary: The requesting client SHOULD retry the request at the new address(es) given by the Contact header field (Section 20.10). Defined in rfc 3265.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x400_Bad_Request
member.summary: The request could not be understood due to malformed syntax. The Reason-Phrase SHOULD identify the syntax problem in more detail, for example, "Missing Call-ID header field".

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x401_Unauthorized
member.summary: The request requires user authentication.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x403_Forbidden
member.summary: The server understood the request, but is refusing to fulfill it. Authorization will not help, and the request SHOULD NOT be repeated.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x404_Not_Found
member.summary: The server has definitive information that the user does not exist at the domain specified in the Request-URI.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x405_Method_Not_Allowed
member.summary: The method specified in the Request-Line is understood, but not allowed for the address identified by the Request-URI.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x406_Not_Acceptable
member.summary: The resource identified by the request is only capable of generating response entities that have content characteristics not acceptable according to the Accept header field sent in the request.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x407_Proxy_Authentication_Required
member.summary: This code is similar to 401 (Unauthorized), but indicates that the client MUST first authenticate itself with the proxy.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x408_Request_Timeout
member.summary: The server could not produce a response within a suitable amount of time, for example, if it could not determine the location of the user in time.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x410_Gone
member.summary: The requested resource is no longer available at the server and no forwarding address is known. This condition is expected to be considered permanent.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x412_Conditional_Request_Failed
member.summary: Is used to indicate that the precondition given for the request has failed. Defined in rfc 3903.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x413_Request_Entity_Too_Large
member.summary: The server is refusing to process a request because the request entity-body is larger than the server is willing or able to process. The server MAY close the connection to prevent the client from continuing the request.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x414_RequestURI_Too_Long
member.summary: The server is refusing to service the request because the Request-URI is longer than the server is willing to interpret.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x415_Unsupported_Media_Type
member.summary: The server is refusing to service the request because the message body of the request is in a format not supported by the server for the requested method. The server MUST return a list of acceptable formats using the Accept, Accept-Encoding, or Accept-Language header field, depending on the specific problem with the content.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x416_Unsupported_URI_Scheme
member.summary: The server cannot process the request because the scheme of the URI in the Request-URI is unknown to the server.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x417_Unknown_Resource_Priority
member.summary: TODO: add description. Defined in rfc 4412.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x420_Bad_Extension
member.summary: The server did not understand the protocol extension specified in a Proxy-Require or Require header field.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x421_Extension_Required
member.summary: The UAS needs a particular extension to process the request, but this extension is not listed in a Supported header field in the request. Responses with this status code MUST contain a Require header field listing the required extensions.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x422_Session_Interval_Too_Small
member.summary: It is generated by a UAS or proxy when a request contains a Session-Expires header field with a duration below the minimum timer for the server. The 422 response MUST contain a Min-SE header field with the minimum timer for that server.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x423_Interval_Too_Brief
member.summary: The server is rejecting the request because the expiration time of the resource refreshed by the request is too short. This response can be used by a registrar to reject a registration whose Contact header field expiration time was too small.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x428_Use_Identity_Header
member.summary: It is used when the verifier receives a message with an Identity signature that does not correspond to the digest-string calculated by the verifier. Defined in rfc 4474.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x429_Provide_Referrer_Identity
member.summary: TODO: add description. Defined in rfc 3892.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x436_Bad_Identity_Info
member.summary: It is used when the Identity-Info header contains a URI that cannot be dereferenced by the verifier (either the URI scheme is unsupported by the verifier, or the resource designated by the URI is otherwise unavailable). Defined in rfc 4474.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x437_Unsupported_Certificate
member.summary: It is used when the verifier cannot validate the certificate referenced by the URI of the Identity-Info header, because, for example, the certificate is self-signed, or signed by a root certificate authority for whom the verifier does not possess a root certificate. Defined in rfc 4474.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x438_Invalid_Identity_Header
member.summary: It is used when the verifier receives a message with an Identity signature that does not correspond to the digest-string calculated by the verifier. Defined in rfc 4474.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x480_Temporarily_Unavailable
member.summary: The callee's end system was contacted successfully but the callee is currently unavailable (for example, is not logged in, logged in but in a state that precludes communication with the callee, or has activated the "do not disturb" feature).

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x481_Call_Transaction_Does_Not_Exist
member.summary: This status indicates that the UAS received a request that does not match any existing dialog or transaction.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x482_Loop_Detected
member.summary: The server has detected a loop.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x483_Too_Many_Hops
member.summary: The server received a request that contains a Max-Forwards.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x484_Address_Incomplete
member.summary: The server received a request with a Request-URI that was incomplete. Additional information SHOULD be provided in the reason phrase.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x485_Ambiguous
member.summary: The Request-URI was ambiguous.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x486_Busy_Here
member.summary: The callee's end system was contacted successfully, but the callee is currently not willing or able to take additional calls at this end system. The response MAY indicate a better time to call in the Retry-After header field.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x487_Request_Terminated
member.summary: The request was terminated by a BYE or CANCEL request. This response is never returned for a CANCEL request itself.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x488_Not_Acceptable_Here
member.summary: The response has the same meaning as 606 (Not Acceptable), but only applies to the specific resource addressed by the Request-URI and the request may succeed elsewhere.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x489_Bad_Event
member.summary: Is used to indicate that the server did not understand the event package specified in a "Event" header field. Defined in rfc 3265.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x491_Request_Pending
member.summary: The request was received by a UAS that had a pending request within the same dialog.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x493_Undecipherable
member.summary: The request was received by a UAS that contained an encrypted MIME body for which the recipient does not possess or will not provide an appropriate decryption key.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x494_Security_Agreement_Required
member.summary: TODO: add description. Defined in rfc 3329.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x500_Server_Internal_Error
member.summary: The server encountered an unexpected condition that prevented it from fulfilling the request.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x501_Not_Implemented
member.summary: The server does not support the functionality required to fulfill the request.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x502_Bad_Gateway
member.summary: The server, while acting as a gateway or proxy, received an invalid response from the downstream server it accessed in attempting to fulfill the request.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x503_Service_Unavailable
member.summary: The server is temporarily unable to process the request due to a temporary overloading or maintenance of the server.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x504_Timeout
member.summary: The server did not receive a timely response from an external server it accessed in attempting to process the request.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x504_Version_Not_Supported
member.summary: The server does not support, or refuses to support, the SIP protocol version that was used in the request.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x513_Message_Too_Large
member.summary: The server was unable to process the request since the message length exceeded its capabilities.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x580_Precondition_Failure
member.summary: When a UAS, acting as an answerer, cannot or is not willing to meet the preconditions in the offer. Defined in rfc 3312.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x600_Busy_Everywhere
member.summary: The callee's end system was contacted successfully but the callee is busy and does not wish to take the call at this time.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x603_Decline
member.summary: The callee's machine was successfully contacted but the user explicitly does not wish to or cannot participate.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x604_Does_Not_Exist_Anywhere
member.summary: The server has authoritative information that the user indicated in the Request-URI does not exist anywhere

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.SIP.Stack.SIP_ResponseCodes.x606_Not_Acceptable
member.summary: The user's agent was contacted successfully but some aspects of the session description such as the requested media, bandwidth, or addressing style were not acceptable.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Client.SMTP_Client
member.summary:
Provides a full SMTP client implementation for sending email messages over SMTP or ESMTP. The class supports connection setup, greeting handling, capability discovery, optional TLS upgrade via STARTTLS, optional authentication, envelope commands, and message transmission.
The client can be used in both simple one‑shot scenarios (via QuickSend and QuickSendAsync) or in advanced manual mode where each SMTP command is issued explicitly. It supports sending messages from streams or from instances.
The implementation follows RFC 5321 and related extensions, including EHLO feature parsing, SIZE support, and STARTTLS negotiation.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Client.SMTP_Client.#ctor
member.summary: Default constructor.

member.summary: Clean up any resources being used.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Client.SMTP_Client.OnConnectedAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Performs SMTP‑specific post‑connection initialization after the underlying TCP connection (and optional SSL/TLS negotiation) has completed. This method reads the server's initial greeting banner and validates that the server has accepted the connection with a 220 reply code.
member.param: A token that may be used to cancel the asynchronous read operation.

remarks.para: According to RFC 5321 4.2, an SMTP server must send a greeting immediately after the connection is established. The greeting may consist of a single 220 line or a multi‑line 220‑ sequence followed by a final 220 line.

If the greeting indicates success, this method stores the greeting text and initializes internal SMTP session state such as the ESMTP feature list and the per‑message recipient collection. If the server does not return a 220 reply code, an is thrown.
The base implementation in performs no actions; this override provides the SMTP‑specific behavior required to begin a valid SMTP session.

member.returns: A task representing the asynchronous post‑connection operation.
member.exception: Thrown when the server's initial greeting does not contain a 220 reply code, indicating that the SMTP session cannot proceed.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Client.SMTP_Client.Disconnect
member.summary: Disconnects from the SMTP server and sends the QUIT command before closing the connection.
member.exception: Thrown if the client instance has already been disposed.
Thrown if the client is not currently connected.
member.remarks: This override always performs a graceful disconnect by invoking with true, causing the SMTP QUIT command to be sent before the connection is terminated.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Client.SMTP_Client.Disconnect(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Disconnects from the SMTP server and optionally sends the QUIT command before closing the connection.
member.param: If true, the method sends the SMTP QUIT command before terminating the connection.
member.exception: Thrown if the client instance has already been disposed.
Thrown if the client is not currently connected.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Client.SMTP_Client.DisconnectAsync(System.Boolean,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Disconnects from the SMTP server and optionally sends the QUIT command before closing the connection.
member.param: If true, the method sends the SMTP QUIT command before terminating the connection.
A token that may be used to cancel the asynchronous read operation.
member.exception: Thrown if the client instance has already been disposed.
Thrown if the client is not currently connected.
member.remarks:
When is true, the method attempts to send the QUIT command and read the server's final reply. Any exceptions raised during this final exchange are suppressed, and the connection is closed regardless.
All SMTP session state (greeting text, host names, ESMTP capabilities, sender and recipient information, and authenticated identity) is cleared before the underlying connection is closed.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Client.SMTP_Client.EhloHelo(System.String)
member.summary: Synchronously sends the SMTP EHLO command using the specified host name and reads any ESMTP features advertised by the server. If the server does not accept EHLO, the method automatically falls back to the HELO command.
member.param: The host to present to the server.
member.exception: Thrown if the client instance has already been disposed.
Thrown if the client is not connected.
Thrown if is null.
Thrown if is an empty string.
Thrown when both EHLO and HELO fail to receive a successful 250 reply from the server.
member.remarks: This method blocks the calling thread until the greeting sequence completes. When the server accepts EHLO, the asynchronous implementation extracts the server's greeting domain and stores all advertised ESMTP extension lines. If the server does not support EHLO, the method falls back to HELO to establish a basic SMTP session.
member.returns: The SMTP reply produced by the remote endpoint. The returned contains all reply lines and the final reply code that represents the outcome of the operation.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Client.SMTP_Client.EhloHeloAsync(System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Sends the SMTP EHLO command using the specified host name and reads any ESMTP features advertised by the server. If the server does not accept EHLO, the method automatically falls back to the HELO command.
member.param: The host name to present to the server.
A token that may be used to cancel the asynchronous read operation.
member.exception: Thrown if the client instance has already been disposed.
Thrown if the client is not connected.
Thrown if is null.
Thrown if is an empty string.
Thrown when both EHLO and HELO fail to receive a successful 250 reply from the server.

remarks.para: When the server accepts EHLO, this method extracts the server's greeting domain and reads all advertised ESMTP extension lines. These features are stored internally and can be used to determine server capabilities such as authentication methods, size limits, pipelining, and other SMTP extensions.
If the server does not support EHLO, the method falls back to HELO to establish a basic SMTP session.

member.returns: A task that completes with the SMTP reply produced by the remote endpoint. The returned contains all reply lines and the final reply code that represents the outcome of the operation.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Client.SMTP_Client.MailFrom(System.String,System.Int64,LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.SMTP_t_DSN_Ret,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Sends the SMTP MAIL FROM command using the specified sender address and optional ESMTP extension parameters.
member.param: The sender email address supplied to the SMTP server in the MAIL FROM command. This value may differ from the address specified in the message's From: header. Specify an empty string to use the null reverse-path ("<>").

The message size in bytes. A value less than or equal to zero indicates that no SIZE parameter should be sent. The SIZE parameter is included only when the server advertises support for the extension and a positive value is specified.
The delivery status notification return option. The default value is . This parameter is included only when the server advertises support for the DSN extension.

An optional envelope identifier associated with the message for delivery status notification tracking. The default value is null. This parameter is included only when specified and the server advertises support for the DSN extension.

Specifies whether the SMTPUTF8 parameter, defined by RFC 6531, should be included in the MAIL FROM command. The default value is false.
Set this parameter to true when internationalized email addresses containing non-ASCII characters are used in the MAIL FROM or RCPT TO commands. For example, the address jüri@example.com requires SMTPUTF8.
When true, the SMTPUTF8 parameter is always sent. No capability check is performed by this method. If the server does not support the SMTPUTF8 extension, it is expected to reject the command.
member.exception: Thrown if the client instance has already been disposed.
Thrown if the client is not connected or if EHLO or HELO has not been issued before calling this method.
Thrown if is null.
Thrown when the server rejects the MAIL FROM command and does not return a successful 250 reply.

remarks.para: This method blocks the calling thread until the SMTP operation completes.

This method is a synchronous wrapper around
and provides identical behavior.
If the command succeeds, the specified MAIL FROM address is stored internally and becomes the current sender address for subsequent RCPT TO and message transfer commands.

member.returns: The server response to the MAIL FROM command. The returned contains the complete SMTP reply, including all reply lines and the final reply code.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Client.SMTP_Client.ReadResponseAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Reads a complete SMTP server response consisting of one or more reply lines.
member.param: A token that may be used to cancel the asynchronous read operation.
member.returns: A instance containing all reply lines returned by the server, including any continuation lines and the final reply line.
member.exception: Thrown when the client instance has already been disposed.
Thrown when the underlying TCP stream is null.
Thrown when the SMTP server closes the connection before a complete reply is received.
Thrown when the server returns more than the allowed maximum number of reply lines (100), indicating an excessively large or malformed multi‑line reply.
member.remarks:
This method reads SMTP reply lines until the final reply line is encountered, as defined in RFC 5321 section 4.2.
A multi‑line SMTP reply consists of one or more lines that begin with the same 3‑digit reply code. Continuation lines use the reply-code "-" format, and the final line uses reply-code SP followed by the reply text.
Each line is parsed into an instance, including optional enhanced status codes (RFC 3463 / RFC 5248) when present.
When the terminating reply line is read, the method returns an containing all collected reply lines.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_e_MessageStoringBegin
member.summary: Provides data for the MessageStoringBeginAsync event, which is raised when the SMTP session begins receiving message content via the DATA or BDAT command. The event allows the application to supply a writable stream where the incoming message bytes will be stored.
member.remarks:
The event is raised once per message, before any DATA body lines or BDAT chunks are processed. The application may assign a custom writable stream to to control how the message is stored.
If the application does not assign a stream, the server will either allocate a default hybrid memory/file stream or reject the command, depending on the configured storage policy. BDAT requires a storage sink from the first chunk, therefore omitting a stream does not prevent the server from accepting BDAT chunks; the server may internally route them to a discard sink if the message is to be rejected at BDAT LAST.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_e_MessageStoringBegin.#ctor(LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_Session)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class using the specified SMTP session.
member.param: The SMTP session associated with the message‑storing operation.
member.exception: Thrown when is null.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_e_MessageStoringBegin.Session
member.summary: Gets the active associated with the command that raised this event. Provides access to session‑level information such as connection state, security status, local endpoint, and server capabilities.
member.value: The instance that is currently processing the SMTP command.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_e_MessageStoringBegin.StoreStream
member.summary: Gets or sets the writable stream into which the incoming message content will be stored. The application may assign any writable instance (memory, file, database, etc.).
member.remarks:
This property must not be set to null. If the application does not assign a stream during MessageStoringBeginAsync, the server will automatically allocate a default hybrid memory/file stream to ensure correct handling of both DATA and BDAT transports.
BDAT requires a storage sink from the first chunk, therefore rejecting the command when no stream is provided is not permitted by RFC 3030. The server will always allocate a fallback stream if none is supplied.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_e_MessageStoringCancel
member.summary: Provides data for the MessageStoringCancelAsync event, which is raised when the SMTP session aborts the message‑storing operation before completion. Cancellation may occur if the client closes the connection, the message size exceeds the server's configured limit, a DATA line exceeds the permitted length, or the session times out during message reception.
member.remarks:
This event is raised after the server has determined that the message cannot be accepted but before returning the final SMTP response to the client.
The property contains any message data that was received prior to cancellation. Depending on the failure condition, the stream may contain partial content, truncated data, or discarded bytes. The message is not delivered and does not enter normal processing.
Applications may use this event for logging, diagnostics, or inspection of the partial message content.
