member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class using the specified SMTP session and the stream containing the message data that was received before the storing operation was cancelled.
member.param: The SMTP session associated with the cancelled message‑storing operation.
The stream containing any message data that was received prior to cancellation. This may contain partial or discarded content depending on the reason for the cancellation.
member.exception: Thrown when or is null.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_e_MessageStoringCancel.Session
member.summary: Gets the active associated with the command that raised this event. Provides access to session‑level information such as connection state, security status, local endpoint, and server capabilities.
member.value: The instance that is currently processing the SMTP command.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_e_MessageStoringCancel.Stream
member.summary: Gets the stream containing any message data that was received before the message‑storing operation was cancelled.
member.remarks:
The stream may contain partial message content or discarded data depending on the reason for cancellation (for example, a DATA line exceeding the permitted length, a BDAT chunk violation, or a server‑side policy rejection).
The stream is provided for diagnostic, logging, or inspection purposes. It does not represent a complete or valid message.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_e_MessageStoringComplete
member.summary: Provides data for the MessageStoringCompletedAsync event, which is raised when the SMTP session has finished receiving all message content via the DATA or BDAT command. The event supplies the completed message stream and allows the application to override the final SMTP response returned to the client.
member.remarks:
This event is raised after the terminating DATA period (.) or the final BDAT chunk marked with LAST. At this point the message stream contains the full message data and is ready for inspection, storage, or further processing.
The property contains the server's default final reply (typically 250 OK), but event handlers may replace it with a custom instance to reject the message or to provide alternative success or failure text.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_Session.EhloAsync
member.summary: Occurs when the server receives the EHLO command from the client. The event is raised after the command syntax has been validated but before the server sends its 250 reply lines. Handlers may inspect the session, modify the default , add or remove advertised SMTP extensions, or reject the EHLO command by returning an error response.
member.remarks: The event provides full access to the parsed EHLO domain and the server-generated reply lines. Applications may customize the advertised capabilities (for example, conditionally exposing AUTH mechanisms only when TLS is active) or override the response entirely.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_Session.HeloAsync
member.summary: Occurs when the server receives the HELO command from the client. The event is raised after the command syntax has been validated but before the server sends its 250 reply. Handlers may inspect the session, modify the default , or reject the HELO command by returning an error response.
member.remarks: HELO is the simple greeting command defined by RFC 5321. Unlike EHLO, it does not negotiate extensions. Applications may use this event to customize the greeting reply or enforce connection policies before the session proceeds.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_Session.MailFromAsync
member.summary: Occurs when the server receives the MAIL FROM command. The event is raised after the command syntax and address have been parsed but before the server sends its reply. Handlers may inspect the sender address, apply acceptance policies, modify the default , or reject the MAIL FROM command by returning an error response.
member.remarks: The MAIL FROM command initializes a new message transaction. This event provides access to the envelope sender, optional parameters (such as SIZE or BODY), and the current SMTP session state. The application may enforce sender validation, rate limits, size limits, or other policies before the transaction proceeds.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_Session.RcptToAsync
member.summary: Occurs when the server receives the RCPT TO command. The event is raised after the command syntax, address, and parameters have been parsed but before the server sends its reply. Handlers may inspect the recipient address, apply acceptance policies, modify the default , or reject the RCPT TO command by returning an error response.
member.remarks: The RCPT TO command adds a recipient to the current message transaction. This event provides access to the envelope recipient, optional parameters (such as NOTIFY or ORCPT), and the current SMTP session state. Applications may enforce recipient validation, forwarding rules, relay restrictions, quota limits, or other policies before the recipient is accepted.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_Session.MessageStoringBeginAsync
member.summary: Occurs when the server is about to begin receiving message content for a DATA or BDAT command. The event is raised after the command has been accepted and before any message data is read. No server reply is sent at this stage, and the message transfer cannot be aborted here. Handlers may inspect the session and initialize storage resources in preparation for reading the message content.
member.remarks: For DATA, this event is raised immediately after the server has sent the 354 reply and before the first byte of message data is read. For BDAT, it is raised after the BDAT command is parsed and accepted. The application may allocate buffers, open storage streams, or perform other initialization tasks required for processing the incoming data.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_Session.MessageStoringCancelAsync
member.summary: Occurs when the server aborts a DATA or BDAT message transfer before completion. This event is raised if the client closes the connection, the session times out while reading message data, or the incoming message exceeds the server's configured maximum size. The transfer cannot continue once this event is raised.
member.remarks: The event is triggered during the message data phase, after the server has begun reading content but before a successful terminating sequence (CRLF.CRLF for DATA or the final BDAT chunk) is received. Handlers may inspect any partial message data that was collected and perform cleanup or logging. The server will send the appropriate SMTP error reply after the handler returns.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_Session.MessageStoringCompleteAsync
member.summary: Occurs when the server has successfully finished receiving all message content for a DATA or BDAT command. The event is raised after the terminating sequence (CRLF.CRLF for DATA or the final BDAT chunk) has been fully read and before the server sends its final reply. Handlers may inspect the completed message data, perform final processing, or reject the message by returning a non-success .
member.remarks: This event indicates a normal, successful end of the message data phase. For DATA, it is raised after the terminating dot sequence is received. For BDAT, it is raised after the last chunk marked with the LAST flag has been completely read. Applications may finalize storage, commit the message to a queue, update metadata, or reject the message before the server sends its final acceptance response.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_t_RcptTo
member.summary: Represents a parsed RCPT TO envelope recipient and any associated DSN (Delivery Status Notification) parameters as defined in RFC 3461.
member.remarks: This type contains the forward‑path mailbox specified in the RCPT TO command, the DSN NOTIFY settings that determine when delivery status notifications should be generated, and the optional ORCPT value that identifies the original recipient. These values correspond directly to the parameters supplied by the SMTP client during the RCPT TO stage of an SMTP transaction.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_t_RcptTo.#ctor(System.String,LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.SMTP_t_DSN_Notify,System.String)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class, representing the parsed RCPT TO envelope recipient and any DSN (Delivery Status Notification) parameters supplied with the command.
member.param: The forward‑path mailbox extracted from the RCPT TO command. This value identifies the envelope recipient and must not be null.

The DSN NOTIFY value associated with the recipient, as defined in RFC 3461. This flag set indicates under which conditions a delivery status notification should be generated:
Success — notify on successful delivery.
Failure — notify on delivery failure.
Delay — notify on delayed delivery.
Never — no DSN should be generated under any circumstances. This value must not be combined with any other NOTIFY flags.
NotSpecified — the NOTIFY parameter was not supplied in the RCPT TO command. When absent, servers may interpret this as either FAILURE or FAILURE,DELAY for compatibility with clients that do not implement DSN extensions.

The optional ORCPT (original recipient) value defined in RFC 3461. When present, it specifies the original recipient address in the form type;address (for example: rfc822;alias@example.com). May be null if the ORCPT parameter was not supplied.
member.exception: Thrown if is null.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_t_RcptTo.Mailbox

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_t_RcptTo.Domain
member.summary: Gets the domain portion of the recipient mailbox.
member.remarks: The domain is extracted from the value by taking the portion following the '@' character. For example, the mailbox user@example.com returns example.com. If the mailbox does not contain a domain part, an empty string is returned.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_t_RcptTo.Notify
member.summary: Gets the DSN NOTIFY value associated with this recipient, as defined in RFC 3461. The NOTIFY setting determines under which conditions a delivery status notification should be generated.
member.remarks:
The NOTIFY parameter may specify one or more of the following values: Success, Failure, Delay. These may be combined unless Never is used. When Never is specified, it must not be combined with any other flags and indicates that no DSN should be generated under any circumstances.
If the NOTIFY parameter is not present in the RCPT TO command, the value is NotSpecified. In this case, servers may interpret the absence of NOTIFY as either Failure or Failure,Delay for compatibility with clients that do not implement DSN extensions.

member.name: P:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.Server.SMTP_t_RcptTo.ORCPT
member.summary: Gets the optional ORCPT (original recipient) value supplied with the RCPT TO command, as defined in RFC 3461.
member.remarks: The ORCPT parameter specifies the original recipient address in the form type;address (for example: rfc822;alias@example.com). This value is present only when the client includes an ORCPT argument in the RCPT TO command; otherwise the property is null.

member.name: T:LumiSoft.Net.SMTP.SMTP_t_EnhancedStatusCode
member.summary: Represents an SMTP Enhanced Status Code as defined in RFC 3463 and RFC 5248. Enhanced status codes provide machine‑readable diagnostic information for both successful and failed SMTP operations, using the structured format class.subject.detail (for example: 2.1.5, 4.4.2, 5.1.1).

remarks.para: Enhanced status codes extend the traditional 3‑digit SMTP reply codes by providing additional semantic detail. They allow clients to distinguish between transient failures (4.x.x), permanent failures (5.x.x), and successful operations (2.x.x), and to identify the specific subsystem involved (addressing, mailbox, network, protocol, content, or security).
The three components of an enhanced status code have the following meaning:

item.description: Class — Indicates success (2), transient failure (4), or permanent failure (5).
Subject — Identifies the functional area (addressing, mailbox, mail system, network, protocol, content, or security).
Detail — Provides fine‑grained diagnostic information within the subject category.

remarks.para: This class stores the parsed components and exposes the raw string form via . Use to construct an instance from a server‑provided enhanced status code.

member.summary: Specifies UDP network type.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.STUN.Client.STUN_NetType.UdpBlocked
member.summary: UDP is always blocked.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.STUN.Client.STUN_NetType.OpenInternet
member.summary: No NAT, public IP, no firewall.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.STUN.Client.STUN_NetType.SymmetricUdpFirewall
member.summary: No NAT, public IP, but symmetric UDP firewall.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.STUN.Client.STUN_NetType.FullCone
member.summary: A full cone NAT is one where all requests from the same internal IP address and port are mapped to the same external IP address and port. Furthermore, any external host can send a packet to the internal host, by sending a packet to the mapped external address.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.STUN.Client.STUN_NetType.RestrictedCone
member.summary: A restricted cone NAT is one where all requests from the same internal IP address and port are mapped to the same external IP address and port. Unlike a full cone NAT, an external host (with IP address X) can send a packet to the internal host only if the internal host had previously sent a packet to IP address X.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.STUN.Client.STUN_NetType.PortRestrictedCone
member.summary: A port restricted cone NAT is like a restricted cone NAT, but the restriction includes port numbers. Specifically, an external host can send a packet, with source IP address X and source port P, to the internal host only if the internal host had previously sent a packet to IP address X and port P.

member.name: F:LumiSoft.Net.STUN.Client.STUN_NetType.Symmetric
member.summary: A symmetric NAT is one where all requests from the same internal IP address and port, to a specific destination IP address and port, are mapped to the same external IP address and port. If the same host sends a packet with the same source address and port, but to a different destination, a different mapping is used. Furthermore, only the external host that receives a packet can send a UDP packet back to the internal host.

member.summary: Resolves the specified host name to a set of IP addresses, optionally filters them based on the provided local endpoint or desired address family, and then initiates an asynchronous TCP connection attempt using the resulting address list.

remarks.para: When a is supplied, its takes precedence and all DNS results are filtered to match it. This ensures that the connection uses the same protocol family as the bound local endpoint.
If is null, the method applies the filter only when it is explicitly set to (IPv4) or (IPv6). When is provided, no filtering is performed and all DNS results are used.
After filtering, the method fails fast if no usable addresses remain, preventing ambiguous or delayed fallback behavior.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.TCP.TCP_Client.ConnectSocks5(System.Net.IPEndPoint,System.String,System.Int32,System.Net.Sockets.AddressFamily,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.Int32)
member.summary: Establishes a TCP connection through a SOCKS5 proxy, resolving the proxy server from a hostname and performing the operation synchronously. This overload performs DNS resolution on and filters the resulting IP addresses based on either the provided or the specified . Optional SOCKS5 username/password authentication is supported.
member.param: Optional local endpoint to bind the underlying socket to. If provided, its address family determines which resolved proxy addresses are eligible for connection.
The hostname of the SOCKS5 proxy server. DNS resolution is performed to obtain one or more IP addresses for connection.
The TCP port of the SOCKS5 proxy server. Must be between 1 and 65535.
The preferred address family (IPv4 or IPv6) to use when is not specified. If is provided, this parameter is ignored.
Optional SOCKS5 authentication username. If both and are provided, SOCKS5 username/password authentication (RFC 1929) will be performed.
Optional SOCKS5 authentication password. Used together with to perform SOCKS5 username/password authentication when required by the proxy.
The destination host name to connect to through the SOCKS5 tunnel. This value is sent to the proxy as part of the SOCKS5 CONNECT request.
The destination TCP port to connect to through the tunnel. Must be between 1 and 65535.

remarks.para: DNS resolution is performed on . If is provided, only addresses matching its address family are used. Otherwise, the parameter determines whether IPv4 or IPv6 addresses are selected.
If and are provided, SOCKS5 username/password authentication (RFC 1929) is attempted. If the proxy requires authentication and the credentials are missing or invalid, the connection will fail.
Once the SOCKS5 CONNECT command succeeds, a raw TCP tunnel is established to :. Protocols such as SMTP, IMAP, POP3, FTP, SSH, and TLS/STARTTLS can be used normally through the tunnel.

member.summary: Establishes a TCP connection to a remote server through a SOCKS5 proxy, performing the full SOCKS5 handshake, optional username/password authentication, and the CONNECT command. The proxy resolves the target hostname and opens the outbound connection on behalf of the client.

remarks.para: This method connects to the specified SOCKS5 proxy using the provided and . After establishing the TCP connection, it performs the SOCKS5 greeting, negotiates an authentication method, optionally executes RFC 1929 username/password authentication, and finally issues the SOCKS5 CONNECT command for and .

When the CONNECT request uses a domain name (ATYP = 0x03), the SOCKS5 proxy performs DNS resolution. The client does not resolve locally. This allows the proxy to handle DNS lookups according to its own network environment, privacy policies, or routing rules.
After the proxy successfully establishes the outbound connection and then invokes to signal that the tunnel is fully established.

member.param: Optional local endpoint to bind before connecting to the SOCKS5 proxy. If specified, its must match the proxy address family.
One or more IP addresses of the SOCKS5 proxy. The method attempts connection in the order provided.
The TCP port of the SOCKS5 proxy.
Optional username for SOCKS5 username/password authentication (RFC 1929).
Optional password for SOCKS5 username/password authentication (RFC 1929).
The hostname of the final destination server. This value is sent to the proxy as a domain name, and the proxy performs DNS resolution.
The TCP port of the final destination server.
A token that may be used to cancel the asynchronous read operation.
member.returns: A task representing the asynchronous SOCKS5 connection and handshake process.
member.exception: Thrown when is null.
Thrown when contains no usable addresses.
Thrown when is outside the valid range (1–65535).
Thrown when the SOCKS5 proxy rejects authentication, fails the CONNECT command, or returns an invalid protocol response.
Thrown when the client instance has already been disposed.
Thrown when the client is already connected.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.TCP.TCP_Client.ConnectHttpConnect(System.Net.IPEndPoint,System.String,System.Int32,System.Net.Sockets.AddressFamily,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.Int32,System.Boolean,System.Net.Security.SslClientAuthenticationOptions)
member.summary: Establishes a TCP tunnel through an HTTP or HTTPS proxy using the HTTP CONNECT method, resolving the proxy server from a hostname and performing the operation synchronously. This overload performs DNS resolution on and filters the resulting IP addresses based on either the provided or the specified .
member.param: Optional local endpoint to bind the underlying socket to. If provided, its address family determines which resolved proxy addresses are eligible for connection.
The hostname of the proxy server. DNS resolution is performed to obtain one or more IP addresses for connection.
The TCP port of the proxy server. Must be between 1 and 65535.
The preferred address family (IPv4 or IPv6) to use when is not specified. If is provided, this parameter is ignored.
Optional proxy authentication username. If both and are provided, a Proxy-Authorization: Basic header will be included in the CONNECT request.
Optional proxy authentication password. Used together with to generate the Proxy-Authorization header for proxies requiring Basic authentication.
The destination host name to connect to through the HTTP CONNECT tunnel. This value is sent to the proxy as part of the CONNECT request.
The destination TCP port to connect to through the tunnel. Must be between 1 and 65535.
If true, the connection to the proxy will be wrapped in TLS using before sending the CONNECT request. If false, the CONNECT request is sent over a plaintext TCP connection.
Optional TLS configuration used when is true. If null, reasonable defaults will be applied. The must specify a valid .

remarks.para: DNS resolution is performed on . If is provided, only addresses matching its address family are used. Otherwise, the parameter determines whether IPv4 or IPv6 addresses are selected.

When is true, the proxy connection is protected with TLS. The CONNECT request is sent inside the encrypted TLS session. After the proxy returns 200 Connection Established, the proxy stops interpreting data and a raw TCP tunnel is created inside the TLS session.

When is false, the CONNECT request is sent over plaintext TCP. After the proxy returns 200 Connection Established, the proxy stops interpreting data and a raw TCP tunnel is created over the plaintext connection.
If and are provided, the method includes a Proxy-Authorization: Basic header in the CONNECT request. This is the standard authentication mechanism for HTTP proxies requiring credentials.

In all cases, once the tunnel is established, the underlying stream behaves exactly as if it were directly connected to :. Protocols such as SMTP, IMAP, POP3, and TLS/STARTTLS can be used normally through the tunnel.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.TCP.TCP_ServerSession.DisconnectAsync
member.summary: Terminates the active session and raises the event if it has subscribers. If the session is already disposed or has been previously terminated, the method returns immediately without performing further actions.

remarks.para: This method marks the session as terminated, invokes the asynchronous event handler (if present), and then disposes the session. The event is invoked with because no protocol‑specific disconnect metadata is provided at the base class level.
Derived server implementations may override or extend this behavior to perform protocol‑specific cleanup, logging, or final message exchange before the session is closed.
Calling this method multiple times is safe; subsequent calls exit early based on the m_IsDisposed and m_IsTerminated flags.

member.returns: A representing the asynchronous disconnect operation.

member.name: E:LumiSoft.Net.TCP.TCP_ServerSession.ErrorAsync
member.summary:
Asynchronous error notification event for the session.
The server raises this event when an exception occurs inside the session processing pipeline. The event provides the exception details through an instance and awaits the subscriber's returned , allowing the handler to perform asynchronous logging, diagnostics, or cleanup.
This event supports only a single subscriber. If more than one handler is attached, the server will reject the subscription to ensure predictable async behavior and to prevent multicast delegate issues where only the last handler's would be awaited.
If no handler is attached, the event is skipped and the exception is not processed further by the session.

member.name: M:LumiSoft.Net.TCP.TCP_ServerSession.OnErrorAsync(System.Exception)
member.summary:
Raises the event when an exception occurs inside the TCP session processing pipeline.
This method wraps the exception into an instance and invokes the asynchronous handler if one is attached. The server awaits the handler's returned , allowing the subscriber to perform asynchronous logging, cleanup, or diagnostics.
member.param: The exception that occurred.
